items.title: French supermarket cyberattack looks like nation-state, says SentinelOne
items.summary: Discover what's happening in retail today, Retail Times publishes international & UK retail news covering products, data, tech, packaging, people, research, comment and much more. Tom Hegel, threat researcher and research lead at cybersecurity platform SentinelOne, believes the French supermarket refrigeration cyberattack looks similar to nation-state level cyber operations aiming to disrupt and sabotage Europe. He believes we’re likely to see this kind of attack on refrigeration again as it hurts very quickly and very publicly and, as we’ve seen […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! Retail Times - Retail Times, a free to view retail news website
items.body:
Tom Hegel, threat researcher and research lead at cybersecurity platform SentinelOne, believes the French supermarket refrigeration cyberattack looks similar to nation-state level cyber operations aiming to disrupt and sabotage Europe. He believes we’re likely to see this kind of attack on refrigeration again as it hurts very quickly and very publicly and, as we’ve seen from so many attacks this week, retail is an incredibly easy target
“These types of attacks typically fall into three main categories: ransomware extortion, political/ideological hacktivism, or nation-state level cyber operations. Ransomware groups usually try to get paid, and hacktivists usually want the public credit. In this case, neither has happened which makes it start to look like the low-cost, deniable sabotage Europe has been dealing with for several years, from damaged undersea cables to warehouse arson and GPS jamming.
“We saw a similar pattern at US military commissaries in August, when freezers on several bases failed within a day of each other and military investigators opened cases. We can’t say the two incidents are linked. What they share is the target: refrigeration controllers that sit on the internet, often running old firmware with publicly known security vulnerabilities.
“That’s also why attribution is so hard here. An attacker who logs into an exposed control panel leaves almost nothing behind, with no malware to analyse and few clues beyond an IP address that probably leads to a rented server. A teenager and an intelligence service would look much the same from the defender’s side.
“Retail is an easy target because retail chains run enormous estates of refrigeration controllers, building management systems, door access panels and point-of-sale gear, much of it installed by facilities contractors who rarely loop in the security team. Grocery margins are thin and stock perishes within hours, so any disruption hurts quickly and in public. The gap between a nuisance and a serious incident often comes down to how much control a victim has exposed to the internet. With thousands of these interfaces still online, I expect more incidents like this.
“Retailers don’t need to know who did it before they act. They should take these controllers off the public internet, put vendor access behind strong authentication, and replace units that no longer get security updates.

items.title: Mid-life shoppers are UK’s most financially pressured and least loyal, research shows
items.summary: Loyalty to both retailers and brands is weakest among 45-54-year-olds as just 35% of the age group describe themselves as financially comfortable, according to new research from IGD. IGD's shopper research shows financial pressure peaks in mid-life, with housing costs and bills consuming almost half… This story continues at Mid-life shoppers are UK’s most financially pressured and least loyal, research shows Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
IGD’s shopper research shows financial pressure peaks in mid-life, with housing costs and bills consuming almost half (49%) of monthly spending among 45-54-year-olds.
In comparison, 46% of both 18-24 and 25-34-year-olds describe themselves as financially comfortable, with household bills taking up 32% and 34% respectively.
At the same time, loyalty to grocery retailers falls to 55% among 55-64-year-olds, the lowest level of any age group, while loyalty to grocery brands reaches its lowest point among 45-54-year-olds at 51%.
Caroline Young, head of shopper insight at IGD, said: “Many mid-life shoppers are becoming the ‘sandwich generation’, balancing mortgages, rising household bills, children and ageing parents.
“What this means for retailers and brands is mid-life shoppers need the strongest reassurance that they’re spending their money well. That’s balancing price with quality, freshness, availability and reliability, rather than competing on price alone.”
IGD’s research shows pressure intensifies through mid-life as shoppers juggle multiple financial and caring responsibilities.
Among 45-54-year-olds, 23% are caring for children under 18, while 18% are also caring for parents or parents-in-law. The combination of housing costs, family responsibilities and wider financial pressures leaves many consumers balancing competing demands on their time and budgets.
Financial confidence follows a similar pattern. Shopper confidence remains positive among younger adults before turning negative after age 45, highlighting a clear divide in financial outlook across age groups.
IGD’s findings suggest value is increasingly becoming a retention strategy rather than an acquisition strategy.
Shoppers aged 45-64 are among the most focused on keeping costs down, but they are also more likely than average to try to balance cost with quality rather than simply buy the cheapest products available.
The research indicates that value is increasingly linked to trust, reliability and helping households make stretched budgets go further.
For financially pressured shoppers, value extends beyond price. Products that last longer, reduce waste and are reliably available are becoming increasingly important measures of whether a purchase represents good value.
The research also finds that shoppers with caring responsibilities are significantly more likely than non-carers to be dissatisfied with product availability, highlighting the growing importance of reliability alongside price.
While these pressures are visible among mid-life shoppers today, IGD believes they may provide an early indication of how value expectations are likely to evolve across the wider grocery market.
With the UK’s 65+ population forecast to grow from 13.8 million to 16.2 million by 2035, needs such as value, quality, freshness and availability are likely to become increasingly influential across the wider grocery market.
Highlights from IGD’s report, ‘What will matter to shoppers in 2035’ can be seen here.

items.title: Bank of England and IMF bosses issue stark warning on cyber threat to trust
items.summary: Andrew Bailey and Kristalina Georgieva voice concerns about financial system on panel about online fraud Business live – latest updates The heads of the Bank of England and the International Monetary Fund have issued a stark warning that rising cyber-attacks risk undermining trust in the financial system. Speaking on a panel about online fraud at the IMF and World Bank meetings in Bangkok, the governor of the Bank of England, Andrew Bailey, pointed to alarming headlines about self-replicating AI agents hijacking personal devices , and the French supermarket hack that heated fridges up to 50C . Continue reading...
items.body:
The heads of the Bank of England and the International Monetary Fund have issued a stark warning that rising cyber-attacks risk undermining trust in the financial system.
Speaking on a panel about online fraud at the IMF and World Bank meetings in Bangkok, the governor of the Bank of England, Andrew Bailey, pointed to alarming headlines about self-replicating AI agents hijacking personal devices, and the French supermarket hack that heated fridges up to 50C.
“If you try to say what’s at the heart of this debate about AI – for me, it’s about trust in technology and it’s about human control to achieve that trust in technology,” he said.
Pointing to the key importance of technology in underpinning today’s financial system, he added: “If we don’t have trust in money, we don’t operate as a society.”
Echoing his concerns, the IMF’s managing director, Kristalina Georgieva, said the toll of cyber-fraud was now so great that people could decide to opt out of the formal financial system altogether.
“I was born and grew up on the other side of the iron curtain,” the Bulgarian economist said. “We didn’t trust the system. What did we do? I would have my dollars in a shoebox under my bed.
“And I worry, today, that unless we figure out how to get ahead of this curve, given the speed, the scale and the cost of fraud growing up, we may end up with lots of people with shoeboxes under their beds.”
She said this threat was particularly acute for people on the fringes of the financial system. “Imagine what would happen if trust disappears or is eroded to a point that people no more have the courage to be included,” she said.
Her comments followed a warning from the IMF on Tuesday that the possibility of a big cyber-attack was one of the factors raising the global financial stability threat level to “elevated”, alongside higher borrowing costs and the risk of an AI share price crash.
Bailey stressed that fraud was now frequently committed via social media platforms and apps, not just traditional financial channels – and urged big tech to take responsibility.
He contrasted today’s environment with the legal status in the UK of outlets such as newspapers, which are responsible for the veracity of everything they publish.
Instead, the governor said: “We’ve moved into quite an extreme position of, well, these platforms are open to everybody and there’s no real liability to the provision of the platform to what’s on it. Guess what? Everything’s on it. You know, the good, the bad and the incredibly ugly and downright criminal and terrible.”
He added: “I don’t go around pointing the finger at people and saying: ‘You’re bad.’ What I have said is: ‘Look, there is responsibility all around.’ And we need to evolve to a world where everybody understands this responsibility, and everybody is then a part of addressing the problem.”
He added: “We must get the social media companies involved because a lot of this fraud is transmitted through those channels.”
Bailey called for the same tools that are being used by cybercriminals to be put to work protecting the financial system. “I’m going to use a sporting metaphor: this technology is arming the offence but it can also arm the defence, and it must do.”
The panel event at which the pair were speaking was to launch a new set of international principles for avoiding cyber-fraud in financial institutions, called the Bangkok blueprint.

items.body:
TimsTims has gained a five-strong listing in selected Tesco stores nationwide and is available now. The award-winning, independent British dairy brand celebrated for its authentic Greek heritage will be rolling out its deliciously creamy, gut friendly Greek Family Natural and Vanilla Kefir alongside premium Greek Family bio-live Vanilla and Raspberry yogurts. Additionally, and exclusively to Tesco, a brand-new Ginger Greek Family Yogurt completes the lineup.
Supplied in 450g recycled card pots with no plastic over-lid (the company was the first in the category to do away with these) the portfolio will launch in Tesco stores for an initial limited-time deal, ending 17th November 2026. Both Natural and Vanilla Kefir flavours will retail for £1.85 while Tims’ 450g Greek Family Yogurt range will be available for £1.75 per pot.
The Tesco partnership follows on from listings in Waitrose, Ocado, ASDA, Sainsbury’s, Booths, along with independents and farm shops. Tims MD Tony Hinds calls this latest development with the high street giant “hugely significant” commenting: “We’re excited to be stocked in the UK’s biggest supermarket and to bring our award-winning delicious range to Tesco shoppers. We’re also excited to introduce our new Ginger Greek Family yogurt as an exclusive to Tesco, our latest recipe made using all-natural stem ginger. The Tesco listing is a hugely significant moment for the Tims business, it is both testament to the dedication of our hard-working team and also represents the continuation of a journey beginning back in the 1940’s that is now step-changing into a new era of availability.”
Greek Family Kefir
Created for moments of healthier indulgence, Tims Greek Family Kefir is lactose, gluten and GM free, suitable for vegetarians, made with 12 gut-friendly live cultures and is supplied in both Natural and Vanilla, both accredited with a two-star Great Taste Award. Unlike thinner, drinkable kefir, Tims has crafted a creamy and luxurious texture by combining the probiotic properties of traditional kefir with its signature thick Greek Family yogurt.
Bio-Live Greek Family Yogurt
Luxurious, rich and creamy and made using fresh British milk sourced from the West Country and the best natural ingredients, the Tims range of Greek Family yogurt is pure, fresh and healthy while being irresistibly moreish. The Vanilla and Raspberry yogurts are both Great Taste Award winners, while the entire range is gluten and GM free, and made with 3 live cultures.

items.title: SEPHORiA London to reveal the trends shaping beauty’s future
items.summary: Discover what's happening in retail today, Retail Times publishes international & UK retail news covering products, data, tech, packaging, people, research, comment and much more. This October, Sephora will bring SEPHORiA Europe to London for the very first time; transforming the iconic creative hub 180 Studios into the ultimate immersive beauty experience that brings together brands, founders, experts and the trends that are shaping what’s next in beauty. Taking place on 16-17th October 2026, SEPHORiA London is the ultimate expression […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! Retail Times - Retail Times, a free to view retail news website
items.body:
This October, Sephora will bring SEPHORiA Europe to London for the very first time; transforming the iconic creative hub 180 Studios into the ultimate immersive beauty experience that brings together brands, founders, experts and the trends that are shaping what’s next in beauty.
Taking place on 16-17th October 2026, SEPHORiA London is the ultimate expression of Sephora’s commitment to bringing their community of beauty lovers together to create unforgettable experiences and fuel the excitement of discovery. For two days, guests attending this in-demand event will be able to discover, touch, test, play, learn and most importantly, connect, with more than 40 brands through interactive activations, workshops, special live shows, exclusive collaborations and plenty of surprise-and-delight moments along the way.
Following editions all around the world, London is ready to put its own distinctive stamp on SEPHORiA. SEPHORiA will tap into the creativity, culture and energy of its host city, inviting customers to discover beauty trends, new launches and cult-favourite brand experiences in distinct neighbourhoods that celebrate the vibrant spirit of London: the Theatre District, the Underground District, and the Residential District.
SEPHORiA London arrives at an exciting moment for Sephora in the UK as the retailer continues to supercharge its growth in the country with new store locations and the exciting announcement of a new strategic partnership with M&S due to launch in Spring 2027.
An immersive journey through the trends. See it. Try It. Experience what’s next.
As experts in brand and production curation, SEPHORiA London will bring guests on a journey through some of the movements that Sephora sees shaping the beauty trends of today and tomorrow. Throughout the neighbourhoods, guests will be invited to journey through a trend-led experience that touches on some of beauty’s most exciting trends today – hyper-personalisation, Asian beauty, next generation innovation, and of course beauty services. Attendees will be able to get hands-on with the products, rituals and ideas behind these exciting new trends, turning beauty discovery into something physical, social and shareable.
Guests will also be able to get bespoke product recommendations with Sephora’s new ‘Beauty Scan’ technology, which assesses a client’s skin to deliver insights well beyond what an app-only solution could provide, including showing clients oil & hydration levels for skin care-based needs, as well as offering more precise shade matching advice for foundation.
On makeup trends, SEPHORiA will feature bold and creative programming designed to inspire and delight guests from trend-forward brands like Charlotte Tilbury, Danessa Myricks and Marc Jacobs Beauty to celebrate makeup in all its expressive glory.
On the wellness front, SEPHORiA will shine a light on inner beauty & wellness through a unique experience created with mindful movement community SANCTUM, offering an immersive take on the growing connection between wellbeing and self-care. Throughout the event days, Sanctum will be providing 12- minute energiser sessions reflective of its signature immersive experience, as well as self-guided meditations and immersive audio experience called “Beauty is Energy,” developed in partnership with Sephora.
The SEPHORA PRIZE for European Incubation : Meet beauty’s next big thing
Sephora has long had its finger on the pulse of emerging brands that have the potential to evolve the future of beauty. These brands are often reflected in stores through dedicated spaces, including ‘Hot On Social’ and ‘The Next Big Thing’. At SEPHORiA London, that spirit of discovery will take centre stage. This spring, Sephora Europe launched the SEPHORA Prize, a new initiative dedicated to discovering the most promising European beauty brands and founders by offering them opportunity to grow and scale with the power of Sephora in Europe.
Forming one of the biggest moments of SEPHORiA’s first night celebration will be the live reveal of the SEPHORA Prize winners during a dedicated award ceremony, celebrating the creativity, innovation and entrepreneurial talent shaping beauty’s next chapter. The 1st winner will receive unparalleled support from Sephora Europe for three years to accelerate its development, which includes dedicated research and development guidance, expert mentoring sessions and extensive visibility sponsorship across all touchpoints. The two other winners will count having a full year of support from Sephora, offering them significant visibility across our Sephora platforms along with mentoring focused on market trends and strategic guidance.
Following the reveal of the winners, all guests attending SEPHORiA London will have the exclusive opportunity to be the first to discover the winning brands and its products within Sephora’s The “Next Big Thing” space at the event.
“Here it is”! Step inside Sephora’s Holiday Campaign
On the heels of Sephora Europe’s groundbreaking Holiday campaign launch featuring beloved international singer, John Legend, SEPHORiA London will provide the exclusive chance of the season to discover the campaign’s festive magic in real life in a dedicated immserive area within the event.
Conceived and art-directed by Sephora as a bold expression of Sephora’s cultural relevance and creative ambition, Sephora Europe’s holiday campaign brings together music, movement and emotion to reimagine the holiday season as a moment of joy, connection and shared celebration – all of which will be expressed within SEPHORiA in a dedicated space.
Bringing the creativity and magic of the campaign off the screen and into real life, attendees will be able to immerse themselves in the universe of this year’s holiday campaign by stepping into a recording studio to sing along with “Here It Is,” the original song created exclusively by John Legend for Sephora.
More than 40 brands under one roof
With more than 40 brands present, SEPHORiA London will bring together some of the most virally-loved brands, showcasing exciting newness, gamification, and brand experiences at this edition, which will include Sephora Collection, Aestura, Anua, Byoma, Charlotte Tilbury, Commodity, Erborian, Fenty, Fugazzi, Glow Recipe, Glowery, Goa Organics, Haus Labs Hourglass, Huda Beauty, Indu, Inde Wild, Kayali, Kerastase, Laneige, Le Monde Gourmand, Lightinderm, MAC Cosmetics, Manucurist, Makeup By Mario, Marc Jacobs Beauty, Medik8, Merit, Natasha Denona, New Notes, Obart, Olaplex, One/Size , Ouai, Phlur, Rare Beauty, Saie, Sephora Collection, Shiseido, Sol De Janeiro, Summer Fridays, Tatcha, The 7 Virtues, Yepoda, Yves Saint Laurent Beauty.
Learn from the Experts with SEPHORiA’s Workshops
SEPHORiA will also continue to elevate its programming through immersive 30-minute mini workshops, giving guests the opportunity to engage directly with brands, founders and beauty experts through interactive formats. Founders such as Danessa Myricks, Marc Elrick from Byoma, Sarah Lee from Glow Recipe and Geraldine Decaux from LightInderm are slated to appear for the mini workshops, guiding guests
with their beauty insider tips, tricks and advice. Additional mini workshops from newly launched Saie and Yepoda are also scheduled for the event days.
A stronger focus on accessibility
SEPHORiA is all about bringing people together through beauty, and this year Sephora is introducing new ways to help more guests enjoy the experience in a way that feels right for them.
Building on Sephora’s Quiet Hours initiative that rolled out globally for our neurodivergent customers or clients who simply want to bring a dose of calmness to their experience, noise-reducing headphones will be available from the moment guests arrive, offering a reprieve for those who may find busy, high-energy environments overwhelming.
UK wellness partner SANCTUM will also create a dedicated wellness space within SEPHORiA – a place to pause, reset and recharge before diving back into everything the event has to offer. Guests will be invited to explore SANCTUM Digital through guided meditations and immersive audio experiences, including a special Sephora x SANCTUM meditation entitled “Beauty is Energy.”
Unique collaborations and exclusive merchandising
As a testament to celebrating the creative spirit of London, SEPHORiA has partnered with a number of noteworthy fashion and lifestyle brands to bring a truly local touch to the global event.
Award-winning British designer ASHISH has created an exclusive merchandise collaboration for SEPHORiA, while TREATS Studios, known for their playful, nostalgic personalised accessories, has created a SEPHORiA version of its virally loved alphabet charms, which will available for purchase at the event.
During the event, attendees will also get to discover some of London’s buzziest names to hit the food and beverage scene. Premium Japanese matcha brand MATCHADO will be serving up a vegan menu of matcha oat lattes and matcha sorbet, with a complimentary vegan matcha chocolate chip cookie included with every latte or sorbet purchase.
Game-changing hydration brand PUNCHY will also sample flavours of its beloved flavours that are packed with electrolytes, minerals and vitamins C and D. Award-winning Lost Sheep ICED Coffee will also sample its zero-caffeine fibre drink in a can, a first for the UK market.

items.title: B&Q expands fast fulfilment options with Deliveroo expansion, and launch of TradePoint Express for trade customers
items.summary: Discover what's happening in retail today, Retail Times publishes international & UK retail news covering products, data, tech, packaging, people, research, comment and much more. B&Q, the UK’s leading home improvement retailer, is strengthening its on-demand delivery offer with the launch of TradePoint Express, a new same-day delivery service exclusively for trade customers, as well as the expansion of its Deliveroo partnership to more than 100 stores nationwide. The latest developments form part of B&Q’s continued investment in giving customers […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! items.body:
B&Q, the UK’s leading home improvement retailer, is strengthening its on-demand delivery offer with the launch of TradePoint Express, a new same-day delivery service exclusively for trade customers, as well as the expansion of its Deliveroo partnership to more than 100 stores nationwide.
The latest developments form part of B&Q’s continued investment in giving customers faster and more convenient ways to access the products they need. Building on recent enhancements including the introduction of Marketplace Click + Collect, customers can now choose from an expanding range of collection and delivery options designed to suit planned projects, urgent repairs and last-minute requirements.
In partnership with on-demand courier platform Gophr, TradePoint Express enables TradePoint Business Development Managers to arrange deliveries, either within two hours or a pre-booked two-hour slot same-day, for TradePoint members from B&Q’s standalone TradePoint store in Barking and 123 participating B&Q stores across the UK. The service is set to expand to moreTradePoint stores later this year, helping even more trade customers save valuable time by reducing the need to travel to collect essential materials and enabling them to stay focused on the job at hand.
B&Q has also expanded its Deliveroo partnership to more than 100 stores nationwide following a successful trial. Customers can now access up to more than 9,000 home improvement products through Deliveroo, with orders delivered in as little as 35 minutes. Since launching in 2024, the Deliveroo partnership has continued to grow in response to increasing demand for fast and convenient access to home improvement essentials, supporting both planned projects and last-minute repairs.
Together, these services are designed to make it easier for both trade and retail customers to access the products they need, whenever and wherever they need them.
Amélie Gallichan-Todd, supply & logistics director at B&Q, said: “We’re continually evolving the ways customers can shop with B&Q, making it faster and more convenient to access the products they need. The launch of TradePoint Express and the expansion of Deliveroo to more than 100 stores are important steps in that journey, giving both trade and retail customers greater flexibility through a range of delivery options designed to suit different project needs. As our customer expectations continue to evolve, we’re focused on making it easier for them to get the right products, exactly when and where they need them.”
Suzy McClintock, VP of consumer at Deliveroo, said: “Deliveroo customers frequently use the platform for their home improvement needs, as they seek out quick and convenient delivery during those DIY emergencies. By expanding our successful partnership with B&Q nationwide, more customers than ever can keep those home improvement projects moving, with access to what they need, when they need it. Whether it’s paint or power tools, we can have them delivered to your doorstep in as little as 25 minutes.”
John Morgan, director of TradePoint, said: “Time is one of the most valuable resources for trade professionals. TradePoint Express has been designed to help our members spend less time collecting materials and more time focused on the job. By working with our TradePoint Business Development Managers and Gophr, we’re providing a flexible same-day delivery service that helps keep projects moving and supports customers when timing matters most.”
Graham Smith, commercial director at Gophr said: “Gophr’s partnership with B&Q, supporting the launch of TradePoint Express, will mean a faster, more convenient service for trade customers. Our technology and delivery network enable flexible, same-day fulfillment that meets the needs of busy professionals, helping products move quickly and efficiently from store to site.”

Premium European coffee house brand, Caffè Nero has partnered with MyProtein, the UK and Europe’s No. 1 Sports Nutrition Brand and part of the global THG Nutrition portfolio, to launch two new protein-based drinks across Caffè Nero’s full UK estate for the first time. The two premium drinks, Iced Vanilla Protein Matcha Latte and the […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! Retail Times - Retail Times, a free to view retail news website
items.body:
Premium European coffee house brand, Caffè Nero has partnered with MyProtein, the UK and Europe’s No. 1 Sports Nutrition Brand and part of the global THG Nutrition portfolio, to launch two new protein-based drinks across Caffè Nero’s full UK estate for the first time.
The two premium drinks, Iced Vanilla Protein Matcha Latte and the Iced Vanilla Protein Latte, are both under 160 calories and both feature 24 grams of protein (in the Matcha Latte) and 25 grams of protein (in the Vanilla Protein Latte), making them two of the highest protein content drinks on the high street.
The Iced Vanilla Protein Latte features Caffè Nero’s award winning Classico coffee blend, skimmed milk, a touch of sweet sugar free vanilla, and a boost of protein. Iced Vanilla Protein Matcha Latte combines smooth, vibrant matcha with skimmed-milk and a touch of sweet sugar free vanilla, and added protein. It is a creamy, refreshing way to enjoy Matcha with a protein boost.
The new drinks support the growing consumer demand for protein, which has become a common part of many people’s daily routine. They also build on the huge popularity of iced drinks in the UK. Iced drinks now account for 14.7% of total drinks sales at Caffè Nero, up from 8.1% five years ago, while iced drinks sales grew by 52% at Caffè Nero in the last financial year versus the previous year.
As with all Caffè Nero’s drinks, each of the new protein drinks will be hand-crafted by baristas, and will also feature MyProtein’s signature protein powder.
The new partnership builds on recent Myprotein launches across UK retail, including a collaboration with Krispy Kreme® to bring a Whey Protein Milkshake inspired by its Original Glazed™ doughnut to Boots, and SNICKERS®, MARS® and Bounty® Impact Whey Protein through its licensing partnership with Mars Wrigley, as the brand continues to expand its offline presence.
The two new drinks at Caffè Nero in the UK are the first launches under the new partnership, with further new recipes due to be announced in January.
Neil Mistry, CEO of THG Nutrition, said: “Protein has moved from the gym bag into everyday life, and coffee is the natural next step. Protein lattes have already taken off in the US, and we know the appetite is here too: our customers already add protein to their coffee at home. Now, with Caffè Nero, they can order it in a latte or matcha on the high street, across more than 600 stores.
“Nero is one of the UK’s best-loved coffee brands, and we’re proud to bring Myprotein to a routine millions of people already enjoy. It’s part of a growing number of food-service partnerships for Myprotein, as protein becomes a staple on menus across the UK, and this is the start of a partnership we’re excited to grow.”
Lysa Hardy, CEO at Caffè Nero UK commented: “The Iced Vanilla Protein Matcha Latte and the Iced Vanilla Protein Latte are delicious, new additions to our menu and respond to growing customer demand for high-protein drinks. They reflect our commitment to innovation and to delivering premium drinks to customers. They combine our speciality, award winning coffee and our ceremonial grade Matcha with the expertise of MyProtein. I think it is a great combination and I can’t wait to for customers to try them!”

items.title: Supermarkets are finding new ways to compete for customers
items.summary: Discover what's happening in retail today, Retail Times publishes international & UK retail news covering products, data, tech, packaging, people, research, comment and much more. Supermarkets have several ways to persuade customers to choose them for their weekly shop. Loyalty prices, discount vouchers, or even money-off experiences are becoming more commonplace and are giving customers more reason than ever to change up their routine. The rise of spend-and-save offers It’s not just supermarkets that are adopting spend-and-save offers. In retail, […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! Retail Times - Retail Times, a free to view retail news website
items.body:
Supermarkets have several ways to persuade customers to choose them for their weekly shop. Loyalty prices, discount vouchers, or even money-off experiences are becoming more commonplace and are giving customers more reason than ever to change up their routine.
The rise of spend-and-save offers
It’s not just supermarkets that are adopting spend-and-save offers. In retail, Dunelm offers 10% off when you spend £20 through the app. They offer free delivery on orders over £60, which gives people an incentive to try the app and then reach the basket value. Sephora is also offering 15% off with the code LOYALTY15. This can be applied to qualifying purchases.
Takeaway services attach discounts to minimum order values. Local apps like Barlick Eats offer a voucher worth 10% of the total value of your last five orders with a takeaway. This encourages loyalty with a single establishment and customer spend, as the money spent directly correlates to the discount given when five orders are placed.
Online bingo sites use related promotions. Bingo promo offers can include 40 free spins when players spend £40, and access to free bingo rooms. This lowers the entry point for people who have never played bingo, and it also offers the chance to play different types of games.
As supermarkets often operate in competitive markets, giving back is the best way to incentivise a customer to try somewhere new. Many shoppers are loyal to a specific supermarket as well, so incentives have to be worthwhile to get someone to switch.
Promotions are also used alongside price matching and own-brand ranges, resulting in a multi-faceted approach that applies savings across whole baskets.
The competition between local supermarkets
Different supermarkets take different approaches to saving. Tesco’s Clubcard Plus costs £7.99 a month and offers subscribers the chance to save 10% off two shops every month. Iceland takes a very different approach, as customers are offered a 10% discount every Tuesday if they are over 60. Both give shoppers a reason to choose them, but at the same time, they encourage different demographics. Sainsbury’s has adopted a more gamified approach.
The supermarket gives shoppers Nectar discounts on their favourite products, with the selection refreshing every week. Games like scratching a virtual scratchcard or entering a prize draw can also be done within the app. Sainsbury’s shoppers can earn Nectar points on certain bonus products too, which contribute to vouchers that can be claimed for money off.
ASDA adopts a similar approach, but instead of having distinctive prices, they translate every penny into a point. By adopting this approach, it becomes easier for each supermarket to target its audience, keeping each one competitive without having to race to the bottom with prices. Spend and save initiatives also work well for customer loyalty, and even though each supermarket is different, there is one common thread.
The terms of saving are clear, and milestones are set. By making the required spend and the reward highly visible, it becomes possible to ensure a transparent process that benefits everyone.

items.title: Costa Express strengthens coffee-to-go offer for retailers with machine upgrades
items.summary: Costa Express has completed a major enhancement programme across more than 13,000 machines nationwide, strengthening its coffee-to-go offer for customers and retail partners. Representing a significant investment across the Costa Express estate, the programme combines recipe, software and machine upgrades designed to improve four key… This story continues at Costa Express strengthens coffee-to-go offer for retailers with machine upgrades Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
Representing a significant investment across the Costa Express estate, the programme combines recipe, software and machine upgrades designed to improve four key areas of the customer experience: drink quality, temperature, cup-fill consistency and speed of service.
Informed by customer insight and machine performance data, improvements introduced across the estate include enhanced recipes for some of Costa Express’s most popular drinks, including the Flat White, alongside changes to drink temperature and cup-fill consistency.
Software upgrades have also reduced dispensing times for selected drinks, helping customers enjoy quality Costa coffee more quickly and conveniently.
Costa Express said the programme is already delivering encouraging results. Earlier phases recorded improvements in drink quality and overall customer satisfaction scores, alongside an uplift in units sold across the Flat White range following the changes.
For retail partners, the enhancements are designed to support greater customer satisfaction and repeat purchase, while strengthening the role that quality coffee can play within convenience, travel and food-to-go destinations.
Mark Cumming, Costa Express director at Costa Coffee, said: “Customer expectations of coffee on the go have never been higher. People rightly expect great-tasting, consistent coffee wherever they choose to enjoy it, whether they’re visiting a coffee shop, travelling, or stopping at their local convenience store.
“Costa Express already operates at significant scale, but leadership means never standing still. We continually listen to our customers, monitor performance, and invest in the parts of the experience that matter most.
“This programme represents a significant investment across more than 13,000 machines, delivering meaningful enhancements to quality, consistency, and convenience.
“We believe convenience should never mean compromising on quality. Our ambition is to continue raising the bar for coffee on the go and make great Costa coffee available to more people, wherever their day takes them.”

items.body:
AI powered marketing platform Miracly publicly launches with $2 million pre-seed funding round
Miracly, a GEO and AI operating system for marketing teams and agencies developed by The Wild Ventures, the company behind Scandinavian home decor brand Wild Palace, has announced a $2 million pre-seed round led by Beenext Ventures and Lotus alongside a Swedish family office, with existing investors including Stefan Lindeberg, Founder at VC firm Creandum; Alex Bouaziz, Founder and CEO at Deel; Thomas Ekman, Founder at 6GAI and former CEO at Axel Johnson publ, Dustin and Tele2; Hedda Baverud Olsson, Founder and CEO at Lassie, and Parham Benisi, Partner at Pophouse.
The company publicly launches today. Pre-launch it has landed customers including Dreams, Acclime, Pixi Beauty, Andy Okay and Duellix.
“We’re seeing an incredible demand for Miracly’s AI marketing platform. Companies all over the world are impacted by decreasing organic traffic from Google and increasing cost of performance marketing,” says Bjorn Bergstrom, Co-founder at Miracly.
“We started out with GEO analytics and AI content generation, but are rapidly becoming a holistic AI marketing platform based on the demand and opportunity we’re seeing in the market. Marketing and agency teams are becoming hybrid marketing and tech organisations and need to develop incredibly quickly to keep up with the changes. Miracly is here to guide them through this shift into an AI first era with completely customised recommendations and agentic flows.”
Co-founders Bergstrom, Arvid Lithander and Shannon Cullum bring to the table backgrounds that include multiple startups and successful exits. And also executive and CEO roles in e-commerce, MarTech, FinTech, consulting and multi-national agency networks such as Saatchi & Saatchi, Wieden+Kennedy, Leo Burnett and MullenLowe.
“As owners of our own brands, we were pitched by agencies that wanted $10,000 just to run an audit of our SEO and GEO. At best they would come up with some recommendations, but we would still have to fix everything ourselves,” says Bergstrom. “At the same time, as consultants and marketing service providers ourselves, we had clients coming to us with the same pain points and no solution. So we built Miracly to fill the void. It offers brand owners a one stop shop that they can put on autopilot. And agencies a platform for better supporting clients and executing against the recommendations they make.”
2026 RTIH Innovation Awards
AI will be a key focus area at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards.
The awards, which celebrate global retail technology innovation in a fast moving omnichannel world, have now closed for entries. Our winners will be revealed at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony, taking place at The HAC in Central London on Wednesday, 4th November.
Check out our 2026 shortlists and finalists here.
We received a record number of entries this year and many fantastic examples of technology excellence driving transformative change across the global retail sector.
Congratulations to all those who made it through the initial submission process! It’s now over to our star studded judging panel who will decide the winners to be announced at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony, taking place at The HAC in Central London.
The event will be held on Wednesday, 4th November and consist of a drinks reception, three course meal, awards ceremony presided over by award winning stand-up comedian, presenter, actor and broadcaster, Aurie Styla, and after party until 1am.
Click here to book your place at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony on Wednesday, 4th November.

items.title: John Healey ‘targets tax crackdown on online marketplaces’ in first budget
items.summary: Move aimed at firms such as Amazon and eBay could raise up to £1bn more for Treasury, says report A tax crackdown on online marketplaces such as Amazon and eBay that could raise up to £1bn more for the Treasury is reportedly being drawn up for John Healey’s first budget. The chancellor is said to be preparing to announce that online marketplaces will be made responsible for collecting tax owed by retailers selling on their platforms. Continue reading...
items.body:
A tax crackdown on online marketplaces such as Amazon and eBay that could raise up to £1bn more for the Treasury is reportedly being drawn up for John Healey’s first budget.
The chancellor is said to be preparing to announce that online marketplaces will be made responsible for collecting tax owed by retailers selling on their platforms.
The move would target foreign retailers that have taken advantage of a lack of robust rules and enforcement to avoid paying VAT on their sales, according to the Times. It said Healey was expected to announce that these changes would be used to fund cuts to business rates for high street shops.
Online marketplaces would be made responsible for collecting VAT at source for all retailers on their platform who have an annual turnover of more than £90,000, it was reported.
The development comes as pressure continues to grow on Andy Burnham and Healey to provide relief to struggling small businesses on the high street before the budget on 28 October.
Before he was elected in Makerfield, Burnham said he would increase the threshold for business rates so that 140,000 small high street retailers would not pay the tax.
While the government faces calls from many factions to cut tax, this week the Institute for Fiscal Studies warned Healey that his budget risks being a “work of fiction” unless he sets out plans to cover £35bn in spending pressures.
The IFS said the damage from higher inflation meant the chancellor would need to either top up funds for his current government spending plans or impose deep real-terms cuts by the end of the decade.
In a boost for the Treasury, this week the International Monetary Fund upgraded its GDP growth forecast for the UK this year to 1.3%, up 0.3 percentage points from its previous update in July.
However the IMF also cautioned that Healey should “stay the course” and continue repairing the UK’s public finances. Silvana Tenreyro, the IMF’s economic counsellor, said the UK “stands out” among G7 countries in having a plan to narrow its deficit.
A spokesperson for the Treasury said: “As has always been the case, decisions on tax are a matter for the chancellor to set out at fiscal events rather than routinely commenting on rumour, speculation or proposals.”

items.body:
chombosan - stock.adobe.com
NatWest uses Nvidia for natural language banking
UK bank is testing Nvidia’s artificial intelligence technology with Royal Bank of Scotland customers
NatWest group is offering customers services through speech recognition technology that will “better understand” and serve them.
Using Nvidia’s artificial intelligence (AI) technology, the bank’s voice-based customer service tool will be able to understand different accents and pronunciations, as well as everyday language concerning money.
The system, known as the Spending Insights Tool, is being tested with 75% of the NatWest Group’s Royal Bank of Scotland customers.
It has been developed by combining Nvidia’s technology with NatWest’s AI research and customer data. “Together, researchers and engineers from both organisations set out to address a challenge facing the next generation of conversational banking services: improving how speech AI understands the wide range of accents, words, phrases and financial language used across the UK,” said the bank.
Spending Insights allows customers to talk naturally about finances using voice and text. They can ask questions about their spending and receive personalised insights. “Customers can interrupt, ask follow-up questions and provide additional context, with the experience combining conversational responses with interactive charts and visualisations,” said NatWest.
Maja Pantic, chief AI research officer at NatWest Group, said customers can interact with the bank “in a way that feels natural to them”.
“If they choose to speak to AI, the technology needs to understand the different accents, words and everyday language used across the UK,” he added.
According to Aser Blanco, global head of banking at Nvidia, the real-time nature of speech recognition makes it challenging. “Working with NatWest has allowed us to apply Nvidia Nemotron open-source models to those real-world banking challenges and identify where the technology can be improved,” he said. “The results show how adapting speech applications to real-world language can make voice experiences more accurate and natural.”
Nvidia Nemotron automatic speech recognition converts spoken words into text, which is then interpreted by NatWest’s proprietary small language models.
Read more about voice AI agents
- Businesses are warming to voice AI agents capable of managing thousands of conversations simultaneously.
- Zendesk’s general manager of customer experience, talks up the rise of voice AI agents, the limits of average handle time and why automated resolution frees human agents.
- From typing to talking: is voice AI finally ready for the enterprise? CIOs need to take natural speech interfaces more seriously.
It was initially tested with 90 NatWest members of staff from different parts of the UK with a variety of accents.
They were asked to not just read scripted questions aloud, but to ask them in their own words, said NatWest, “using the phrases, pronunciations and more informal or colloquial language they would naturally use when talking about their finances”.
NatWest then expanded the work using anonymised contact-centre transcripts, which it said enabled the model to “learn from a much broader range of real-world banking language”.
Voice banking is becoming an increased focus for banks, and they are applying AI to the challenge.
During a recent presentation reported by Computer Weekly, Bahadir Yilmaz, chief analytics officer at ING, said: “Conversational banking, being able to chat with your bank, is going to be a fundamental experience that people will be looking for in the next five years.
“What [ING has] right now is the first baby steps for the conversational AI chatbot, like a little personalised information, problem solving and being able to take an action,” he said. “But we are not that far away from heavy core capabilities, like sending and receiving money, applying for products and getting advice within the boundaries of regulations.”
Last month, digital challenger bank Zopa removed more manual tasks by offering customers the ability to bank through natural speech.
Its customers can now use voice commands to instruct an AI-powered personal digital banking assistant to manage everyday banking tasks, such as making transactions or setting savings goals.
Ask Zopa, as the feature is known, understands and acts on instructions given by customers using conversational language.

items.title: Healey plans £1bn e-commerce crackdown to fund retail tax breaks
items.summary: John Healey is preparing to announce a £1bn tax crackdown on online marketplaces like Amazon and Temu to fund tax cuts for high street shops.  At the Budget later this month, the Chancellor is expected to make e-commerce platforms like Amazon, Ebay and Temu responsible for collecting tax owed by the sellers using their site, [...]
items.body:
Healey plans £1bn e-commerce crackdown to fund retail tax breaks
John Healey is preparing to announce a £1bn tax crackdown on online marketplaces like Amazon and Temu to fund tax cuts for high street shops.
At the Budget later this month, the Chancellor is expected to make e-commerce platforms like Amazon, Ebay and Temu responsible for collecting tax owed by the sellers using their site, the Times has reported.
The Treasury is expected to use revenues from this policy to fund business rates cuts for high street retailers, a move which has long been pledged by Andy Burnham.
This trade-off is likely to be welcomed by retail bosses, who have been ramping up pressure on the government to cut the industry’s soaring tax bill, naming business rates and employment costs among their biggest burdens.
The Chancellor is set to make online marketplaces responsible for collecting VAT at source for each of its sellers whose annual revenue is more than £90,000.
This crackdown will seek to address concerns that foreign retailers are setting up UK shell companies to avoid paying VAT.
Healey will come under pressure to set this threshold lower. Dan Neidle, the founder of Tax Policy Associates, told the Times that this loophole will still be exploited unless the Treasury comes down harder.
“This is a step in the right direction but the Treasury needs to go further and make online marketplaces responsible for collecting every penny of VAT on the sales made on their platform.
“Unless that happens these Chinese sham companies will find just another way around the rules.”
Healey rows back from warehouse tax
During his campaign to become MP for Makerfield, the Prime Minister pledged to exclude 140,000 small high street retailers from business rates to give them “the chance to thrive”.
Burnham had suggested he would hike tax on “out of town” warehouses to pay for this tax break, but retail bosses had been fiercely opposing this proposal.
Hiking tax on warehouses would inevitably push up costs for the retailers using them, eventually resulting in higher prices for consumers, industry leaders had warned.
John Lewis executive chairman Jason Tarry said last week that a warehouse tax would “reveal a fundamental misunderstanding of how modern high streets work”.
The Chancellor is said to have now ruled out a warehouse tax, and his decision to instead pursue online sellers will likely play well with retail bosses, who have often argued that the high street is over-taxed compared to their e-commerce rivals.
Amazon told The Times that it supported the crackdown on online retailers, which it estimated would raise about £700m for the Treasury – lower than the government’s own estimates.
An Amazon spokesman said: “Closing this loophole will raise significant revenue for the exchequer and simplify compliance for both HMRC and legitimate sellers.”
A Treasury spokesperson said: “As has always been the case, decisions on tax are a matter for the chancellor to set out at fiscal events.”

items.title: B&Q and Screwfix CEO: Healey must cut business rates
items.summary: Of all the levers available, reforming business rates presents the single biggest opportunity for the Chancellor to help retailers keep investing, says Thierry Garnier If the Prime Minister wants to deliver growth in every postcode, he can look at the businesses that are already present in every community. Retailers employ 2.75m people across the country [...]
items.body:
B&Q and Screwfix CEO: Healey must cut business rates
Of all the levers available, reforming business rates presents the single biggest opportunity for the Chancellor to help retailers keep investing, says Thierry Garnier
If the Prime Minister wants to deliver growth in every postcode, he can look at the businesses that are already present in every community.
Retailers employ 2.75m people across the country and can support that ambition, but we are facing difficult decisions.
At Kingfisher we are delivering investment through our B&Q and Screwfix stores, creating jobs and supporting local communities across the UK. We are investing in new stores, opening over 20 this year alone. We share the government’s concerns about the number of young people not in employment, education or training (NEET), and we have committed to offering work experience placements at B&Q and Screwfix to help tackle this.
While we want to keep doing this, whether we can depends on what the Chancellor decides in this Budget.
If the government wants growth that people can see in their community, supporting shops is one of the most efficient ways to deliver it.
Business rates remain a heavy burden for shops up and down the country. But large shops are now being impacted by the introduction of a new business rates multiplier, meaning they face the prospect of even higher bills. These stores are anchors in their towns, providing jobs and drawing in customers who then spend elsewhere.
The 20 per cent cut in business rates for pubs, social clubs and live music venues recognised that rates bills are a key factor in whether a local business invests or retreats. The same logic applies to the rest of the UK’s high streets and retail parks
The 20 per cent cut in business rates for pubs, social clubs and live music venues recognised that rates bills are a key factor in whether a local business invests or retreats. The same logic applies to the rest of the UK’s high streets and retail parks.
If the government is committed to its growth strategy, it must reform this long-outdated business rates system and level the playing field between bricks and mortar shops and online-only operators.
We understand the Chancellor faces difficult choices, but with a new administration comes new opportunities for change. Our message to deliver growth is therefore simple: take shops out of paying the higher rate.
These changes matter even more now because rates aren’t the only increased cost we face. In the past 18 months, retailers have absorbed sharp rises in employment, packaging and energy costs, and have worked hard not to pass them on to customers already feeling the squeeze. Every additional cost makes that harder. Of all the levers available, reforming business rates presents the single biggest opportunity for the Chancellor to help retailers keep investing.
We are ready to power growth in every corner of the country.
By choosing to reform business rates, the Chancellor can unlock investment, protect local jobs, and ensure high streets and their local areas remain the beating heart of our communities. The opportunity is clear. Now is the moment to seize it.
Thierry Garnier is chief executive at Kingfisher

items.body:
2026 RTIH Innovation Awards AI Technology (UK) finalists include John Lewis, FoundIt!, Iceland and Snag
We’re pleased to announce the shortlist for the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards AI Technology (UK) category. We received a record number of entries this year and many fantastic examples of technology excellence driving transformative change across the global retail sector.
Check out a rundown of our 2026 shortlists and finalists here.
Congratulations to all those who made it through the initial submission process! It’s now over to our star studded judging panel who will decide the winners to be announced at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony, taking place at The HAC in Central London.
The event will be held on Wednesday, 4th November and consist of a drinks reception, three course meal, awards ceremony presided over by award winning stand-up comedian, presenter, actor and broadcaster, Aurie Styla, and after party until 1am.
Click here to book your place at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony on Wednesday, 4th November.
Our 2026 AI Technology (UK) finalists as follows:
Bodycare and PMC
Bodycare was bought out of administration in 2025 and established an ambitious, innovation driven store opening programme to bring its affordable health and beauty offering back to the high street, with AI central to its comeback.
Its ambition is to become an AI first retailer, running store operations through its own proprietary, custom built AI platform, with AI decisioning powering colleague actions and data captured in-store continuously feeding back to sharpen the platform and performance.
Furniture Connect
Furniture Connect is using AI to make more of a furniture retailer’s existing range commercially viable online. The innovation is not simply generating better product images. The real opportunity is using AI to produce the volume and quality of content retailers need, quickly and consistently, across different ecommerce channels.
Goddiva
Goddiva AI is a proprietary AI powered fashion commerce ecosystem developed to transform how customers discover, select and purchase occasionwear online.
Built using OpenAI GPT, LangChain, Pinecone Vector Database, Python, Django, MySQL and Shopify integration, it combines conversational commerce, semantic product discovery, intelligent personalisation, AI Size Finder, Virtual Try-On and automated customer support within one connected platform.
Beyond the customer journey, Goddiva AI powers bestseller analysis, trend forecasting and product performance prediction. The technology has moved beyond experimentation to deliver measurable commercial impact, generating approximately £2.5 million in AI assisted revenue, increasing conversion from 1.4% to 2.5% and reducing returns by 10%.
Iceland and SAI
Iceland partnered with SAI to harness AI to make its stores smarter, safer and easier to run, tackling shrink while improving colleague productivity and operational performance.
SAI’s AI powered platform transforms existing store data into actionable intelligence, enabling Iceland to identify and respond to loss more effectively while giving colleagues the insight they need to take practical action on the shopfloor.
Rather than remaining a proof of concept, the technology is now playing a significant role in Iceland’s highest shrink stores, helping the retailer target the locations responsible for a disproportionate share of total losses and making stores harder environments for theft.
John Lewis and FoundIt!
John Lewis and FoundIt! deployed genuine, scalable AI to transform retail discovery across a complex 170,000-SKU catalogue. The initiative tackled both sides of the journey: helping customers navigate products through intelligent Visual Navigation, while making relevant ranges more discoverable through automated, intent led SEO.
Together, these complementary capabilities created a powerful discovery flywheel, bringing more relevant shoppers to the site, helping them find products more easily and generating an eight-figure commercial benefit.
Levy and Kappture
Levy and Kappture have together, delivered Europe’s largest frictionless store deployment into Manchester United, with seven BRISK bars operating across the historic Old Trafford.
BRISK is Kappture’s proprietary computer vision technology, transforming the traditional bar experience by allowing fans to enter, select and take their products and leave without stopping at a till. AI powered product recognition automatically identifies purchases, while payment and receipts are processed instantly, significantly reducing queues and increasing customer throughput, as well as delivering an excellent fan experience.
The technology is designed from the ground up to operate at the pace and scale required during live sporting events and its performance demonstrates the impact, with one BRISK store reaching a record 21 transactions in a single minute and processing up to 43 products in the same period compared with a maximum of approximately 10 transactions per minute at a traditional bar.
Minimist
Donated second-hand stock is the hardest inventory in retail for AI to handle. Every item is a one-off with no barcode, no SKU and no product data, arriving in unpredictable condition, so none of the catalogue assumptions that make retail AI work apply.
Minimist turns a single photograph of a donated item into a priced, measured, described listing published across eight marketplaces in 30 seconds, against up to 10 minutes by hand. 89% of listings publish with no human edit at all. 73,844 items have been listed this way by 28 charity retailers across the UK, Ireland and Australia, and 31,580 of them have sold.
Snag and Patchworks
Snag, a size inclusive DTC fashion brand shipping to 100+ countries, has taken AI beyond chat and into live retail operations.
Using Claude as the reasoning layer and Patchworks as the execution layer via MCP, Snag's team now runs product and order operations across multiple Shopify storefronts, five warehouse systems, its PLM, Sage 200 and marketplaces through plain language instructions. Patchworks closed the gaps native AI connectors couldn't: it reached systems with no MCP server and unlocked Shopify's Bulk Operations API.
The result: 14,000+ products updated in a single operation, and one of Snag's fastest ever product launches, delivered in around two weeks.

2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Omnichannel Retail Technology Initiative of the Year finalists announced
We’re pleased to announce the shortlist for the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Omnichannel Retail Initiative of the Year category. We received a record number of entries this year and many fantastic examples of technology excellence driving transformative change across the global retail sector.
Check out a rundown of our 2026 shortlists and finalists here.
Congratulations to all those who made it through the initial submission process! It’s now over to our star studded judging panel who will decide the winners to be announced at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony, taking place at The HAC in Central London.
The event will be held on Wednesday, 4th November and consist of a drinks reception, three course meal, awards ceremony presided over by award winning stand-up comedian, presenter, actor and broadcaster, Aurie Styla, and after party until 1am.
Click here to book your place at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony on Wednesday, 4th November.
Our 2026 Omnichannel Retail Initiative of the Year finalists as follows:
Lyzer
Lyzer is a Lisbon-based logistics-as-a-service (LaaS) platform that gives retailers one system for every channel. It brings orders from stores, online shops and marketplaces into one dashboard, assigns picking and delivery work with smart task allocation, and fulfils each order from the nearest store through click-and-collect, home delivery or both.
Guided picking uses optimised store maps, and route optimisation groups deliveries into efficient clusters. Retailers can turn their existing stores into fulfilment hubs: Staples Portugal now offers same-day delivery within four hours. Lyzer has processed over 1.1 million orders worth more than €330 million in GMV.
SaleDock
Celerant ONE is the evolution of Saledock’s all in one retail platform, created to help independent cycling retailers replace disconnected systems with one powerful solution
It unifies PoS, inventory, e-commerce, workshop management, customer data and supplier integrations, simplifying operations across stores and online channels. Developed through direct collaboration with retailers, the platform is intuitive, scalable and tailored to the realities of cycling retail.
Following Saledock’s 2025 acquisition by Celerant Technology, the launch of Celerant ONE combines Saledock’s UK expertise and local team with greater resources and innovation, while preserving the retailer led mission that has guided the business since its founding in 2019.
Sitoo and Paul Smith
Paul Smith has transformed how its stores connect with the wider customer journey through Sitoo Unified Commerce Platform, anchored by PoS.
Rolled out across 30+ stores in eight countries in three months, the solution connects store teams with inventory, customer and cross-channel information in real time. Customers are recognised and rewarded consistently across stores and online, supported by one customer view shared across systems. Associates can move with customers using mobile Point of Service, access inventory beyond the individual store and support ship-from-store. The result is a more connected experience across physical stores and online.
Stellar Global (Marvesting Group) and Samsung
Stellar, part of Marvesting Group, has supported Samsung for over eight years, designing omnichannel strategies that connect in-store experiences with virtual engagement to boost brand loyalty and ROI. Samsung KX isa 20,000 sq ft flagship in London which has been run by Stellar since opening in 2019.
Within this space, Stellar has built end-to-end customer journeys through immersive product experiences, events, workshops, live broadcasts and virtual engagement. For the February 2026 Galaxy S26 Unpacked launch, Samsung KX was transformed into a Korean street watching party, with Stellar delivering a DTC live broadcast, multi-platform review content and 23 hours of TikTok live shopping. Results included a 24% sales uplift, 100% NPS and six million views.
THG Studios
On 26th February, THG Studios delivered the “world’s first AI driven, immersive, shoppable catwalk”, an officially certified world record achievement.
This project deployed a complete, end-to-end AI ecosystem, moving beyond single point solutions. From AI driven creative concepting and a hybrid human-AI model runway, to the ‘Front Row AI’ app that made the event instantly shoppable, THG Studios closed the gap between inspiration and transaction in seconds. It created a new, commercially proven strategy for brand experience, transforming a live marketing event into a measurable, data rich growth engine and setting a new global standard.
VS Labs
VS Labs is the product and innovation arm of Visualsoft, building Shopify apps and in-store tech that connect e-commerce and physical retail into one unified customer experience.
Launched last year, VS Labs develops solutions around the practical challenges retailers face when connecting customer journeys, data and experiences across channels.

Click here to book your place at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony on Wednesday, 4th November.
Our 2026 Customer Experience Excellence finalists as follows:
Dark’s Bar, Lord’s Cricket Ground
Dark's Bar at Lord’s has transformed hospitality at one of the world’s most iconic sporting venues, combining innovative retail technology with a design sympathetic to Marylebone Cricket Club’s unique heritage.
The solution removes friction from the customer journey while the technology sits quietly in the background, making the experience feel effortless rather than technology led. Faster service and a seamless purchasing journey have contributed to a 35% uplift in units sold. Crucially, innovation has not come at the expense of character: Dark Bar complements the architecture and traditions of Lord’s while meeting modern customer expectations for speed, simplicity and convenience.
Goddiva
Post-Covid, customer expectations have moved beyond simply being able to shop online. Customers increasingly expect digital retail to provide the personalisation, reassurance and individual attention traditionally associated with an in-store experience. Goddiva responded by reimagining occasionwear ecommerce around the individual customer.
AI curated collections adapt around her preferences; intelligent memory recognises her size and past favourites; AI Size Finder helps establish fit; Virtual Try-On lets her see dresses on herself; and personalised alteration recommendations help perfect the final choice. Together, these technologies turn a conventional e-commerce catalogue into an intelligent, evolving digital fitting-room experience designed around each customer.
Hockerty
A Hockerty customer can design a navy suit, a light blue shirt and a camel coat, then see all three on a photo of themselves before a single piece is cut.
That is virtual try-on. Generative AI renders every item in the basket together, from its actual configuration: fabric, cut, colour, lapel, pockets. The same look can be moved to a meeting room, a wedding or a street. It takes 20 to 30 seconds, runs in the browser, and covers the whole range from suits to sneakers, in five languages.
Lloyds Banking Group
Lloyds Rewards is transforming how customers engage with their bank by creating one of the UK's most innovative and rewarding digital experiences.
Available to over ten million eligible customers through Lloyds' digital channels, Rewards combines cashback, challenges, prize draws, retailer discounts and strategic partnerships to help customers save money, discover new brands and be rewarded for everyday activity.
Over the past year, Lloyds has evolved Rewards beyond a traditional cashback proposition into a broader customer engagement platform that delivers meaningful value, greater choice and more personalised experiences. The result is a customer centric innovation that rewards everyday banking in new and engaging ways.
Yours Clothing and Poq
Yours Clothing has worked with poq for seven years, since launching its first native mobile app in 2019.
Rather than treating that success as a one off, Yours Clothing used it as the model for a repeatable, multi-brand mobile commerce strategy: M&Co (2023), Evans (2024), Bad Rhino (2024), Long Tall Sally (2025), Pixie Girl (2025), Yours Clothing Germany (2025), and now the Yours Clothing app (2026) have launched globally on the same proven foundation.
The result is a genuinely scalable approach to omnichannel customer experience - one that delivers a consistently excellent app experience across a diverse portfolio of brands, rather than customer experience excellence being limited to a single flagship.

2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Digital Transformation Project of the Year finalists announced
We’re pleased to announce the shortlist for the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Digital Transformation Project of the Year category. We received a record number of entries this year and many fantastic examples of technology excellence driving transformative change across the global retail sector.
Check out a rundown of our 2026 shortlists and finalists here.
Congratulations to all those who made it through the initial submission process! It’s now over to our star studded judging panel who will decide the winners to be announced at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony, taking place at The HAC in Central London.
The event will be held on Wednesday, 4th November and consist of a drinks reception, three course meal, awards ceremony presided over by award winning stand-up comedian, presenter, actor and broadcaster, Aurie Styla, and after party until 1am.
Click here to book your place at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony on Wednesday, 4th November.
Our 2026 Digital Transformation Project of the Year finalists as follows:
Ann Summers and PMC
Ann Summers partnered with PMC to modernise its core IT infrastructure after years of legacy development had left its tech stack complicated, expensive to maintain and difficult to manage, slowing innovation and creating operational friction.
Dunelm and VoCoVo
Dunelm is transforming its in-store communications infrastructure by upgrading from legacy Series 3 to VoCoVo Series 5 Pro Headsets across its stores. The new devices are elevating customer experience, day-to-day reliability and enabling improved comfort, while creating a platform for AI powered features that change the way colleagues operate and respond to customer queries.
At the same time, VoCoVo has integrated real-time operational alerts with Dunelm’s self-checkouts, sending sub-second alerts to colleagues’ headsets when assistance is needed to reduce void transactions and abandoned purchases.
East of England Co-op and Transaction Network Services (TNS)
East of England Co-op operated more than 200 sites on a fragmented, multi-vendor network with failover times of up to 90 seconds. Working with Transaction Network Services (TNS), the retailer deployed TNS Secure SD-WAN to consolidate its connectivity into a single, resilient platform with built-in redundancy.
Failover is now instantaneous, and the retailer has eliminated visible downtime during network incidents. Centralised dashboards have strengthened compliance and security oversight, while a single managed service has reduced operational complexity and delivered estimated savings of 10-15% through vendor consolidation.
Fortnum & Mason and Proximity
For more than 300 years Fortnum & Mason has been known for exceptional personal service. Earlier this year, Proximity and Fortnum & Mason launched 'Fortnum’s Connect' to bring that service to customers wherever they are.
The platform gives store teams a clear view of each customer’s purchases, preferences and conversations, helping them make relevant recommendations, stay in touch beyond the store and serve customers around the world through remote payments and global delivery. Since launching the platform, Fortnum & Mason has built a client book of more than 1,200 high value customers, whose average transaction value is 630% above the company average.
Intersport Elverys and Rezolve Ai
Intersport Elverys, Ireland’s oldest sports retailer, has transformed its online merchandising in partnership with Rezolve Ai; replacing manual, rules-based work with automated product placement across the site and its search results.
MKM Building Supplies and Commerce
MKM has transformed its digital proposition to make purchasing and account management simpler for trade customers, while strengthening the connection between digital and its nationwide branch network.
Working with Commerce, MKM has built a modern, composable commerce platform designed around complex B2B requirements, including personalised pricing, account terms, credit, quotes, invoices and fulfilment. More than 60,000 SKUs are now available online, while the platform is delivering a 4.1% conversion rate and £125 average order value. By modernising its technology while retaining its service led model, MKM has created a more flexible and connected experience for trade customers.
Paul Smith and Sitoo
Paul Smith transformed its international store technology with Sitoo’s cloud native Unified Commerce Platform, anchored by PoS. Rolled out across 30+ stores in eight countries in three months, the project replaced legacy store technology with a connected platform supporting fixed and mobile selling, real-time inventory visibility, customer recognition and cross-channel operations.
The transformation has changed both the customer experience and everyday store operations: associates can spend more time with customers, transactions are faster, store processes have been simplified and manual administration reduced. The result is a modern store platform designed around how Paul Smith wants its teams to serve customers.
The Body Shop and GoPlaces
The Body Shop had deep high street and direct-to-consumer roots but no operating model for social commerce. So GoPlaces built one. It deployed its technology, OnePlace, for the data foundation, created an affiliate creator network at scale, and ran professional live retail from its studios.
GMV grew 15x from launch to peak month, with 177% month-on-month growth through peak gifting season and more than 27 million affiliate video views across 20,400-plus creator videos. A heritage retailer now trades a channel it had no way of measuring before. For The Body Shop this isn’t just marketing campaigns; it’s a new operating model.
THG Ingenuity
In October 2025, THG Ingenuity and Google Cloud announced a strategic partnership. This focused on combining Google Cloud’s generative AI and data analytics products with THG Ingenuity’s end-to-end commerce and fulfilment capabilities with a goal of accelerating product innovation, delivering step change outcomes for customers, and opening new go to market opportunities.
As part of this, THG Ingenuity committed to move its e-commerce and fulfilment platform from four on-premise datacentres to Google Cloud, combining platform modernisation, governance, and future product growth into one operating model.
WHSmith and SOLUM
WHSmith and SOLUM are supporting a new benchmark for travel essentials retail through Newton Pro electronic shelf labels at WHSmith’s flagship stores across Heathrow Terminals 3, 4 and 5.
The stores bring food, health and beauty, technology, pharmacy services and other essentials together in a one stop shop travel destination. Digital shelf-edge communication enables faster, more consistent pricing and promotional updates, helping travellers navigate with confidence while supporting WHSmith’s ambition to make every journey better.
