items.title: Lidl snaps up market share as rival Aldi stalls
items.summary: Lidl is the fastest-growing grocer in the UK, new figures suggest, as the discount supermarket grabs more market share while its rivals stall. The German discounter held 8.6 per cent of the UK’s grocer market in the 12 weeks to October, according to Worldpanel by Numerator, up from 8.2 per cent a year ago.  This [...]
items.body:
Lidl snaps up market share as rival Aldi stalls
Lidl is the fastest-growing grocer in the UK, new figures suggest, as the discount supermarket grabs more market share while its rivals stall.
The German discounter held 8.6 per cent of the UK’s grocer market in the 12 weeks to October, according to Worldpanel by Numerator, up from 8.2 per cent a year ago.
This makes Lidl the UK’s only supermarket which is actively growing its hold on the market, and comes as the grocer sets out plans to tighten its grip on British shoppers.
Lidl’s sales are 7.1 per cent higher than the same time last year, driven by growth in categories including fruit, vegetables and wine. During the period, the grocer saw half a million more visits than at the same time last year.
Fraser McKevitt, head of retail and consumer insight at Worldpanel, told City AM: “Of the 38 grocery sectors we measure, Lidl is growing ahead of the market in 28. It’s always the large sectors that really move the dial for a retailer’s growth, and Lidl is performing well in fresh produce, alcohol, prepared foods, soft drinks and dairy.”
Lidl is strengthening its loyalty among British shoppers, as 54 per cent of households shopped at the grocer in the last 12 weeks.
The grocer, and its German counterpart Aldi, struggled to impress UK shoppers when they first arrived in the market but have since grown in popularity among middle-class families.
“Loyalty schemes have also become more important to shoppers looking to secure discounts in recent years, and Lidl Plus appears to be resonating, with Lidl reporting a 23 per cent increase in app users over the last year,,” McKevitt said.
Last week, Lidl said its loyalty prices were a key driver of its 10.8 per cent jump in revenue in the year to February, to £13bn. The group’s pre-tax profit grew by a third to £206m. The supermarket has plans to open 50 new stores in the next year.
Asda falls furthest
Aldi, Lidl’s main rival, is the only UK supermarket which does not use loyalty pricing. Its chief executive, Giles Hurley, has hit out at his rivals for supposedly misleading shoppers by using loyalty discounts to inflate the apparent value of savings.
Aldi’s market share slipped from 10.6 to 10.5 per cent in the past 12 months. Hurley has said the grocer is focussed on growing volumes, rather than headline sales, as it attempts to shield shoppers from price rises.
Tesco, the UK’s biggest supermarket, saw its market share fall from 27.9 to 27.8 per cent. Its closest competitor, Sainsbury’s, fell from 15.3 to 15.2 per cent.
Asda suffered the biggest fall in market share, dropping from 11.8 to 11.5 per cent of the market. Former chief executive Allan Leighton returned to the budget supermarket to lead a turnaround in 2024, and said in August the company is in the “foothills of recovery”.
Asda and Morrisons – which held its market share at 8.3 per cent – have both sought to shrink their billion-pound debt piles since being taken over by separate private equity buyers.
A spokesperson for Asda said: “Asda is more than just a supermarket. The business as a whole remains in growth and while the grocery market has slowed in recent weeks, we continue to narrow the gap to competitors.
“This reflects our ongoing investment to lower prices and improve the shopping experience for customers – actions that will build a stronger Asda for the long term.”

items.title: Retailers press Healey to cut high street taxes at crunch Downing St meeting
items.summary: Retailers urged John Healey to “reverse the damage” of rising high street taxes as the Chancellor met industry bosses on Tuesday. Top retailers including Tesco, Sainsbury’s and Marks & Spencer pressed Healey on business rates and youth unemployment but the Chancellor stopped short of confirming any Budget measures.  Healey hosted high street bosses at Number [...]
items.body:
Retailers press Healey to cut high street taxes at crunch Downing St meeting
Retailers urged John Healey to “reverse the damage” of rising high street taxes as the Chancellor met industry bosses on Tuesday.
Top retailers including Tesco, Sainsbury’s and Marks & Spencer pressed Healey on business rates and youth unemployment but the Chancellor stopped short of confirming any Budget measures.
Healey hosted high street bosses at Number 11 Downing Street for a breakfast briefing on Tuesday, amid growing pressure for the government to slash taxes on retailers and hospitality firms.
The retailers in attendance – which also included Co-op – were accompanied by the bosses of industry bodies UK Hospitality (UKH), the British Retail Consortium (BRC) and the British Beauty Council.
Healey used the meeting to emphasise the importance of retailers and hospitality firms to the UK’s economy, as he stressed the “vibrancy of the high street,” according to a Treasury source.
The Chancellor used the meeting to hear from industry bosses about what the government can do to boost investment and secure breathing space for businesses. Healey did not give bosses any insight into his plans for this month’s Budget, it is understood.
Healey urged to reverse ‘years of damage’
BRC chief executive Helen Dickinson, who attended the meeting, said she urged Healey to unwind the tax rises implemented by his predecessor, Rachel Reeves. Her Treasury “whacked up” retailers’ taxes by 20 per cent in two years, including an extra £6.5bn in employment costs, she said.
“The Chancellor recognised these pressures, and we had a positive discussion about our shared ambition for growth and tackling youth unemployment,” Dickinson said.
“His first Budget is the chance to turn that ambition into action by easing costs, making tax fairer and unlocking investment. That is how we get retailers hiring, investing and creating opportunities for the next generation.”
Retail bosses reiterated their calls for Healey to avoid a so-called warehouse tax by hiking business rates on large retailers to pay for tax cuts for smaller firms.
Alongside the tax burden facing high street firms, industry bosses urged Healey to help them employ young people, as the number of under-25s not in education, employment or training (Neet) nears 1m.
UKH chief executive Allen Simpson, who met with Healey on Tuesday, said the summit was “a positive discussion about our shared agenda to fix the NEETs crisis and how the government can reverse the damage of the last two years to get young people back into work.”
“It’s clear to me that hospitality and the high street will hire NEETs in a way the rest of the economy simply cannot. It’s important the Chancellor recognises this and reduces hospitality’s tax burden at the Budget, to allow the sector to create jobs in every postcode,” he added.

items.title: Premier Inn owner brands last two Budgets 'most unfriendly to hospitality ever'
items.summary: The boss of Whitbread has called on the Government to help hotels with 'punitive' business rates and roll back National Insurance changes.
items.body:
Premier Inn owner brands last two Budgets 'most unfriendly to hospitality ever'
The boss of Whitbread has described Labour's two Budgets as the most unfriendly to hospitality ever, as he reiterated calls to roll back National Insurance changes.
Chief executive Dominic Paul said two Budgets had been 'the most unfriendly budget to hospitality that probably the industry has ever seen' after firms were surprised by rate increases alongside hikes to wages and a shock increase to NI employer payments.
He said it had become 'really hard to create as many jobs as we want to when we've got these punitive increases in hotel business rates and employment costs.’
Rolling back the changes to National Insurance would ‘enable us to create new jobs’ and help with the country’s worrying youth unemployment problem, he said.
Whitbread's business rates bill is set to double to £200 million by 2028, and the sector had been ‘hammered’ over the last two Budgets.
He called on Andy Burnham and John Healey to freeze business rate hikes for hotels as he revealed Whitbread's half-year profits were hit by a restructuring plan prompted by last year's tax rises.
He said: ‘We need them to move away from the increases they’ve got planned for the next two years because they’re punitive.
Whitbread has called for support for hotels with business rates at the upcoming Budget
‘We’re actually really supportive of the government’s agenda to get the country back to growth and create jobs. We need the government to help us in order for us to help the country.’
Although pubs and live music venues have been promised a reduction on their business rates bills from next spring, hotels have been furious about their own bills rising over the next few years.
He also hit out at the Government’s proposals for a visitor levy to charge all tourists staying overnight in the UK.
Paul said: ‘This is further taxation on hardworking, highly taxed people in the UK, and there is no clear evidence of how or where that money will be spent, which seems like a very inefficient way of taking money from the general population and then putting it back into the economy.’
The hotel giant has urged investors to reject its third biggest shareholder Corvex's attempts to win a board seat. The US hedge fund holds a stake of around 6.4 per cent in Whitbread, worth around £270 million.
Paul said the company was ‘not credible’ and he had a ‘firm opinion’ on not giving them a board seat. He said Corvex ‘has a changing thesis’ and was serving as a ‘distraction’.
The investor previously urged Whitbread to launch a sales process and then a few months later said it was not ‘demanding a sale of the company.’
It wants Whitbread to split its business into separate hotel operations and real estate companies.
The business, which operates more than 850 hotels across Germany and the UK, said in April it would shut its restaurant business in a move risking 3,800 jobs across the UK and Ireland.
It also announced plans to sell and lease back £1.5 billion of its freehold properties.
Profits for the six months to 27 August fell 62 per cent to £109 million as strong sales were offset by the costs relating to its restructuring and higher costs.

items.title: UK shoppers seek deals as grocery price inflation rises again
items.summary: Price of chocolates falls in run-up to Halloween, while supermarkets use special offers to draw in sales Business live – latest updates Grocery price inflation in the UK has picked up further, prompting shoppers to turn to special offers to keep their bills down – while the price of chocolates has fallen in the run-up to Halloween. Supermarket prices were 2.5% higher than last year in the four weeks to 4 October, up from 2.3% last month, according to data from the retail analysts Worldpanel by Numerator. Continue reading...
items.body:
Grocery price inflation in the UK has picked up further, prompting shoppers to turn to special offers to keep their bills down – while the price of chocolates has fallen in the run-up to Halloween.
Supermarket prices were 2.5% higher than last year in the four weeks to 4 October, up from 2.3% last month, according to data from the retail analysts Worldpanel by Numerator.
Spending on promotions over the last month was more than £250m higher than a year ago, with many shoppers using special offers to keep their grocery bills in check or to make pricier items and larger packs more affordable, Worldpanel said.
Fraser McKevitt, the head of retail and consumer insight at Worldpanel, said: “With the autumn budget fast approaching [on 28 October], the cost of living continues to weigh heavily on the minds of shoppers. And the cost of filling up a car is only adding to the pressure on household budgets.
“More than half tell us they’re very or extremely worried about petrol prices, and almost one in three say it’s already taking a real toll on their finances. Until the chancellor sets out his plans, we expect that caution to carry on showing up at the till, with shoppers leaning more heavily on promotions to keep their grocery spend under control.”
However, in some good news for households stocking up on trick or treat supplies for Halloween, chocolate confectionery prices are 3% lower than a year ago.
About 1.2 million households bought a pumpkin over the latest four weeks, up 10% year on year, while more than 250,000 households treated themselves to a pumpkin spice coffee.
McKevitt added: “Halloween and Christmas are two of the most important moments of the year for chocolate confectionery, so falling prices will be welcome news for shoppers and retailers alike.
“After the double-digit increases of 2025, a 3% drop won’t fully reverse what consumers have paid in recent months, but it should help ease some of the pressure on household budgets as the festive season approaches.”
While sales of hot chocolate and soup surged in September compared with August, by 41% and 35% respectively, they fell sharply when compared with last year, by 20% and 4% respectively.
A separate report from NielsenIQ showed total till sales at major UK supermarkets grew 1.4% in the four weeks to 3 October, down from 1.8% growth in the previous month, as shoppers remain cautious about spending.
Summer favourites remained popular as September was unusually warm this year, with strong sales of mineral water (+17.4%) and ice-cream (+11.7%), while sales of hot chocolate (-11%) and ready-to-eat soup (-5.4%) declined year on year.
Asda was the only big grocer to report a drop in sales, of 0.5%, in the 12 weeks to 4 October, Worldpanel said.
The German discounter Lidl led in market share gains and now controls 8.6%, on the back of a 7.1% increase in sales driven by fruit, vegetables and wine.
Sales at the online grocer Ocado increased by 12.4%, outpacing online sales across the sector at 5.5%.
Spending through the tills was 1% higher at Tesco and 1.3% higher at Sainsbury’s, with the two retailers holding 27.8% and 15.2% of the market respectively.
Asda’s share now stands at 11.5%, while Aldi holds 10.5% of the market, with sales at the discounter up 0.4% year on year.
Beyond the supermarkets, grocery sales at Marks & Spencer rose by 14.9%.

UNiDAYS, the world’s leading verification platform for students, is partnering with one of Britain’s most iconic retailers, Marks & Spencer (M&S).
The partnership gives UNiDAYS’ student community in the UK exclusive access to 15% off M&S’s clothing, home, and beauty ranges. Available for purchases made online, the partnership makes it easier for students to access the retailer’s high-quality products as they build their wardrobes for university, work, and beyond.
The collaboration gives students access to thousands of products across M&S’s own-brand collections alongside more than 100 third-party fashion, beauty, and home brands. M&S has been ranked number one for perceptions of quality and value across all age groups for more than a decade and, last year, became number one for style.
The partnership comes as M&S continues to broaden its appeal, with a 16% increase in under-35s shopping with the brand compared with last year. Through UNiDAYS, M&S will reach more than seven million students and graduates in the UK.
The launch also marks an important step in UNiDAYS’ continued expansion in the UK and its strong partner network across the fashion industry, partnering with some of the biggest brands in the UK, and offering students 100s of discounts in this sector.
Richard Stoker, affiliate partnerships manager at M&S, said: “Partnering with UNiDAYS is a brilliant way for us to introduce more students and recent graduates to M&S and help them discover the style, quality and value we offer across clothing, home and beauty. With an exclusive 15% discount, they can make their money go further as they prepare for university, settle into student life or take their first steps into the world of work.”
Alex Gallagher, chief strategy officer at UNiDAYS, said: “We’re delighted to partner with M&S and help open up one of Britain’s most iconic heritage retailers to students and graduates across the UK. For more than 140 years, M&S has been known for its quality, style, and exceptional value, and we’re excited to make its fashion offering more accessible to the next generation of shoppers.”

items.title: Sluggish sales as shoppers look for Budget boost
items.summary: UK total retail sales increased by 1.3% year on year in September, against a growth of 2.3% in September 2025, according to the BRC-KMPG Retail Sales Monitor. This was below the 12-month average growth of 1.5%. Food sales increased by 2.5% year on year in… This story continues at Sluggish sales as shoppers look for Budget boost Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
This was below the 12-month average growth of 1.5%.
Food sales increased by 2.5% year on year in September and non-food sales increased by 0.3% year on year in September, against a growth of 0.7% in September 2025.
Helen Dickinson, chief executive at the British Retail Consortium (BRC), said: “Retail sales growth remained subdued in September as households are still cautious with their spending ahead of expected rises in household bills and taxes.
“The chancellor cannot promise to ease the cost of living while piling more costs onto the retailers working to keep prices down. With confidence fragile, this Budget is a critical test. Retailers will do everything they can to protect value for customers, but Government must play its part. Another rise in business rates would push up pressure on prices, choke off high-street investment and put local jobs at risk. This Budget must back retail to invest, employ and grow — not make it harder.”
Sarah Bradbury, CEO, IGD, said: “September saw shoppers return to familiar routines as the summer holidays came to an end but despite the greater stability, shopper confidence dipped against a backdrop of surging prices at fuel pumps and planned rises in energy prices. Speculation around tax rises in the Budget will also be weighing on shoppers’ minds, with these factors adding pressure to household finances and translating into weaker spending.
“While Halloween may support impulse grocery sales in the short term, food businesses’ attention will be firmly on the Budget and what it could mean for consumer spending power, business costs and demand heading into 2027.”

items.body:
Taylor’s, the historic Port House, today unveils Taylor’s Special Reserve, a new addition to its range created to bring the distinctive Taylor’s house style to more occasions and more moments of enjoyment.
Launching exclusively in Tesco stores across the UK, Taylor’s Special Reserve broadens the house’s offering with an accessible expression designed for relaxed and informal occasions. Priced at £14, it offers consumers a new way to enjoy Taylor’s, sitting alongside established favourites such as Taylor’s Late Bottled Vintage.
As consumer preferences evolve, Taylor’s is responding by offering greater choice across different occasions and price points, while remaining true to the quality and character for which the house has been known for generations. Whether shared with friends, enjoyed after dinner or simply poured at the end of the day, Special Reserve is designed to make it easier to find an occasion for Taylor’s.
The bottle design pays homage to more than three centuries of Taylor’s heritage, from 1692 to the present day. Presented in the house’s traditional black bottle and finished with a red capsule, Taylor’s historic crest and classic typography, the release draws on the house’s unmistakable visual identity, giving the new expression a strong and recognisably Taylor’s presence on shelf.
A rich, fruit-forward Reserve Ruby Port, Taylor’s Special Reserve combines generous dark fruit flavours with the balance and structure characteristic of the Taylor’s house style. Ready to serve and enjoy straight from the bottle, it is a versatile Port particularly suited to informal gatherings, relaxed evenings at home and an after-dinner glass.
Adrian Bridge, managing director of Taylor’s, says: “Taylor’s has been part of British tables for generations, and we want that to continue. Our Late Bottled Vintage remains a firm favourite, but consumers increasingly want choice across different occasions and price points. Special Reserve gives them another way to enjoy Taylor’s – an accessible, generous Port that is easy to share, while retaining the quality and character people expect from us.”
Taylor’s Special Reserve Port will be available exclusively at Tesco stores across the UK, priced at £14.

items.body:
Tesco Media today announces a new partnership with API-first ad infrastructure provider Kevel, strengthening the technology behind its advertising proposition and giving brands greater flexibility to connect with Tesco customers.
Kevel’s technology powers Tesco Media Ad Manager, a new client-facing platform designed to make planning, booking, measuring and optimising media simpler, more connected and more useful for brands. The technology will play a central role in helping Tesco Media deliver a seamless experience as it continues to develop new advertising formats and capabilities across its digital channels.
The partnership is the latest step in Tesco Media’s investment in making retail media simpler, more effective and more connected for advertisers. By combining Tesco’s first-party customer insights with Kevel’s flexible technology, Tesco Media will be able to develop and launch advertising products more quickly, while maintaining control over customer information and how advertising appears across Tesco’s channels.
For advertisers, this will enable more relevant audience targeting and greater flexibility across formats including sponsored product listings, shoppable display and video, as well as advertising within Scan As You Shop.
It will also allow Tesco Media to respond more quickly to changing advertiser needs and key retail moments, helping brands reach the right audiences with relevant messages throughout the shopping journey.
Stacy Gratz, revenue and growth director at Tesco Media, said: “Retail media works best when it creates value for customers as well as advertisers. This partnership gives us greater flexibility to build advertising experiences around how our customers actually shop, while making it easier for brands to use Tesco’s scale and customer insights effectively.
“Kevel’s technology will help us move faster, develop new capabilities and continue evolving Tesco Media around the needs of our advertisers and customers.”
James Avery, founder and CEO of Kevel, added:“Tesco has a clear vision for the role retail media can play for both its customers and advertising partners. We’re proud that Kevel’s technology will support Tesco Media as it builds the next generation of its advertising proposition, giving its team the flexibility to innovate and develop new experiences at scale.”
Tesco Media reaches millions of customers every week and enables advertisers to use Tesco’s first-party insights to better understand audiences and deliver more relevant campaigns. Customer information will continue to be managed in line with Tesco’s own security, privacy and compliance standards.
Kevel’s technology is being introduced across Tesco Media in phases, with the first advertising placements already live and further capabilities planned across Tesco’s digital ecosystem.

items.title: Business rates relief expansion can unlock hiring and investment, says FSB
items.summary: Expanding business rate relief at the Budget could help more small firms invest, recruit and grow, according to new data from the Federation of Small Businesses (FSB). Almost three in 10 (28%) small employers say they would hire more staff if Small Business Rate Relief… This story continues at Business rates relief expansion can unlock hiring and investment, says FSB Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
Almost three in 10 (28%) small employers say they would hire more staff if Small Business Rate Relief (SBRR) were to be expanded.
Even one in 10 (11%) sole traders would consider taking on a member of staff for the first time if the relief saved them money.
More than a quarter (26%) of small employers would increase employee pay or benefits.
In England, SBRR gives a 100% discount for properties with a rateable value of up to £12,000, with tapered relief up to £15,000. This has remained unchanged for almost 10 years.
Ahead of this month’s Budget, FSB is calling on the chancellor to increase the SBRR threshold to £25,000, which would remove at least 250,000 more small businesses from paying rates, giving them much-needed room to expand and grow.
FSB’s data found over a third (36%) of small businesses say SBRR is essential or important to their business. The figures are even higher for the retail and accommodation and food sectors, where costs are particularly high, with around half of small firms seeing it as essential or important (49% and 47% respectively).
As well as expanding SBRR, FSB is urging the chancellor to:
- Substantially increase the Employment Allowance, then index it in line with the National Living Wage (NLW), so support with employer National Insurance contributions (NICs) keeps pace as wage costs rise and continues to cover at least the NICs of four full-time workers on the NLW. Without that protection, rising employment costs risk putting small firms off hiring, with young people and those with health challenges among those most likely to lose out.
- Cut Business Asset Disposal Relief to 14%, reversing the rise to 18 per cent and restoring the pre-April 2026 rate after higher capital gains taxes weakened incentives for entrepreneurs to expand and grow. The higher rate has already damaged growth intent, making entrepreneurs less willing to expand, invest and take risks on growing their businesses.
- Raise the VAT registration threshold to £100,000, keeping more sole traders and the smallest firms out of a tax that can swallow more than a working week a year in compliance. It also sees firms deliberately restrict turnover to avoid being pulled into the VAT system.
- Remove 75% of Renewables Obligation costs from small business energy bills, giving small firms the same help households have already received and easing the pressure of sharp rises in standing charges and electricity wholesale prices.
- Introduce a Statutory Sick Pay (SSP) rebate for small employers, helping small firms manage rising employment costs and making it easier for them to hire and support people with health conditions.
Tina McKenzie, FSB’s national chair, said: “Small businesses across the UK are up against huge and persistent cost rises that are seeing so many struggle with running their business, let alone investing and expanding. This is the most important opportunity for the Government to make its more pro-small business tone a reality.
“If we are to get the growth needed, the Budget must be a moment for some meaningful action, backing the small firms and self employed that are so crucial to the economy.
“We need a tax system that rewards ambition rather than punishes it. Widen Small Business Rate Relief so fewer firms are dragged into a punishing pre-profit tax, protect the Employment Allowance so hiring does not become steadily more expensive, reverse the damaging rise in Business Asset Disposal Relief and raise the VAT threshold so firms are not deliberately holding back turnover to avoid a cliff edge. These are practical changes that would give small businesses a reason to invest, hire and grow.
“This Budget will be an early test of whether the new Government will put itself on the side of those who run a small business. Ministers say they want growth, but growth does not happen by squeezing margins, making employment more expensive and putting barriers in the way of expansion.
“If the chancellor wants to win back the confidence of entrepreneurs, he should start by making it worthwhile to take a risk again.”

items.body:
TFG London has reported a cybersecurity incident affecting Phase Eight, Hobbs and Whistles this morning. It comes within days of the ASOS breach, which occurred just a few days ago.
Vincent Guillevic, director of fraud labs at Entrust, said: “E-commerce and digital retail organisations like TFG and ASOS operate at the intersection of payments, personal data, digital identities, and customer trust, making them attractive targets for cybercriminals. As retailers become increasingly dependent on cloud services, third-party platforms, and external partners, their attack surface continues to expand. Attackers are increasingly using identity-based account takeover attacks to take over customer and employee accounts.
“For retailers, trust is the foundation before any transaction. Breaches put that trust at risk, with potentially lasting reputational harm and negative impacts on sales. The faster an organisation can investigate, communicate accurately, and demonstrate that it has contained the issue, the better positioned it is to maintain customer confidence and limit long-term reputational or commercial impact.
“Organisations should focus not only on determining the scope of any potential compromise, but also on validating the integrity of customer-facing systems and communications. Security strategies should verify not only access credentials but also the users, devices, and behaviours interacting with critical systems continuously.”
Claud Bilbao, VP, underwriting & distribution, Cowbell, said: “Two cyber incidents hitting major fashion retailers in a matter of days should be a wake-up call for the entire sector. There’s no evidence the attacks are connected, but cybercriminals don’t need to take a retailer offline to inflict serious damage. Stealing customer data, disrupting orders or undermining consumer confidence can be just as costly. And with Black Friday and Christmas approaching, attackers know that retailers face enormous pressure to keep trading. That commercial pressure can become a weapon in the hands of cybercriminals, particularly when they’re looking to extort a business.”
Muhammad Yahya Patel, vCISO and cybersecurity advisor for EMEA at Huntress, said: “Another week, another UK retailer dealing with a cyber incident. What’s confirmed is instructive enough without speculation. Several IT systems became unavailable. Websites were affected. Online orders placed from 11 October may be delayed. The fact that Inside Story and White Stuff within the same group were unaffected, and that TFG’s wider Africa and Australia operations were untouched, suggests some degree of system separation was in place. That separation, which limited the blast radius, is worth noting as a positive. The retail sector’s security problem in 2026 isn’t a lack of awareness. It’s the gap between what organisations know they should do and what they’ve actually done about it. That gap is exactly what attackers are measuring when they choose their next target.”

YAZOO, the UK’s number one flavoured milk brand, has announced it has surpassed £100 million in retail sales value (RSV), cementing its position as a primary driver of growth within the milk drinks category.
This significant milestone has been driven by sizeable distribution gains, particularly within the convenience and discount channels, alongside a strategic focus on accessibility. The brand’s commitment to accessible formats and price points has established YAZOO as a gateway to the category, attracting new shoppers and resonating strongly with its core 18-to-24-year-old demographic.
Building on this momentum, YAZOO is launching a bold new creative campaign, ‘Have a YAZOO with yourself’, backed by a £3 million investment. Running across out-of-home, audio, and digital channels, the campaign uses humorous, relatable scenarios to engage young adults, encouraging them to find a moment of joy amidst everyday chaos.
“YAZOO has always been about bringing joy to consumers’ lives, commented Ali Heal, YAZOO brand manager at FrieslandCampina. “Being a young adult today can be very stressful, so we want YAZOO to provide fun and a moment to sip, reflect and reset.”
Looking ahead, YAZOO is poised to unlock the next wave of growth. Following a major insights project, the brand has developed a new category vision which has identified a potential £600m+ opportunity2. FrieslandCampina is actively sharing this vision with retail partners and preparing to launch an exciting NPD pipeline aligned with these identified growth drivers.
Heal adds: “We are incredibly proud of this milestone and grateful to all our supportive customers. We want our retail partners to feel they’re backing the right brand – one with the ambition, quality and ability to keep delivering for shoppers, while helping the wider category grow. We’re excited to build on this momentum together, with more to come soon.”

Ecommpay, the inclusive global payments platform, has added Klarna, the everyday finance network, to its payment choices, giving merchants a simple way to offer millions of shoppers greater choice, transparency and control at checkout.
“Flexible payment options are fundamental to a strong checkout experience for e-commerce merchants and Klarna has been a popular choice for consumers and businesses,” explained Roman Tazetdinov, head of strategic partnerships, Ecommpay. “Used by millions of shoppers every month, we are confident adding Klarna to the Ecommpay payment platform will deliver real conversion gains for our merchants.”
“Shoppers today expect to pay their way: no faff, no friction, no nasty surprises,” said Klarna country manager UK & Ireland Marc O’Fathaigh. “Ecommpay is a natural fit: we both believe good ways to pay should be available to everyone. Through a single integration, this partnership puts Klarna in front of merchants worldwide, expanding our reach and giving millions of shoppers more control over their money.”
From small businesses to global enterprises across retail, travel and hospitality, fintech, mobility, digital goods and insurance, Ecommpay merchants gain access to Klarna’s flexible payment options including Pay in Full, Pay in 3 and Pay in 4 instalments, Pay in 30 days, and longer-term Financing, via one easy integration with no extra technical work or third-party systems needed.
“We know that many shoppers actively look for Klarna at checkout,” added Roman Tazetdinov. “Adding it to the Ecommpay payment platform gives merchants access to a large and engaged market, reducing hesitation at the point of purchase and giving customers another payment option at checkout. And it can be added to a merchant’s wider payment set-up in a single integration, eliminating unnecessary operational overhead.”

items.title: Phase Eight and Hobbs owner hit by cyber-attack, as H&M probes separate hack claim
items.summary: TFG London has apologised to customers for disruption after it identified a "cybersecurity incident" on Sunday.
items.body:
Phase Eight and Hobbs owner hit by cyber-attack, as H&M probes separate hack claim
- Published
The owner of high-end fashion brands Hobbs, Whistles and Phase Eight says it is investigating a cyber-security incident.
According to TFG London - the UK arm of retail conglomerate The Foschini Group - it identified an incident on Sunday affecting some IT systems and "specifically impacting our Phase Eight, Hobbs, and Whistles brands".
"We are actively investigating and working with external cyber security specialists," the company told BBC News in a statement.
Meanwhile, H&M is investigating a separate claim that it was attacked by a notorious hacking group.
TFG said its brands' stores are operating as normal but some website capabilities may be unavailable, adding "we apologise for any disruption and will provide additional updates to our customers as appropriate".
The retail group reportedly told customers in an email that it did not believe customers' payment information had been affected by the incident.
"As our investigation continues, we will be working to identify if any sensitive information related to our customers was impacted," it said.
The email, seen by news service PA, also said that those whose personal information had been impacted would be informed directly.
"We do not believe it is necessary to change your account login information at this time," it added.
Beverley Griffiths, senior lecturer in security and resilience at Bucks New University told PA that this was "a clear sign that major brands are firmly in the crosshairs of cyber attackers".
Fashion giants ranging from Adidas to Alexander McQueen have been targeted by cyber-criminals seeking to extort money by threatening to release customer data unless they are paid a ransom.
"No organisation is immune, so the real test of resilience is how quickly a business can detect an incident, respond and recover while keeping its customers informed," Griffiths said - adding customers should stay "vigilant" and wary of suspicious messages.
Charlotte Wilson, head of enterprise at cyber-security firm Check Point, said attacks targeting retailers were "starting to look rather like buses... you wait for one, and suddenly three come along at once".
She told the BBC that while it was too soon to ascertain how the incident affecting TFG London's systems occurred, or whether it was related to other recent hacks, "the retail industry has some serious questions to answer about how exposed its systems have become".
H&M investigating hack claim
On Monday, it was also reported that fashion giant H&M was investigating a claim of a hack by a cyber-criminal group called ShinyHunters.
The hackers have been previously linked to high-profile attacks including targeting the FBI, Rockstar Games and Ticketmaster.
"We are aware of information circulating online regarding a potential cyber security incident and are currently investigating the claims," H&M told BBC News in a statement.
"At this time, we have not found any indications that our data environment has been compromised."
It also comes only a week after Asos customers were informed the online fashion and beauty retailer had been hacked by another group, via a push notification appearing on their phone screens.
Cyber-security experts told the BBC it was an unprecedented move for hackers to effectively transform an app notification system into a "ransom note".
It later emerged that hackers had obtained more detailed personal information belonging to Asos customers than the retailer initially suggested.
An update was issued to customers after BBC News told the retailer it had been contacted by cyber criminals who said the breach went beyond the "basic contact details" Asos previously said might have been accessed.

items.title: Hobbs and Phase Eight owner hit by a cyber attack after H&M fears it was targeted
items.summary: The parent company of fashion brands including Hobbs, Phase Eight and Whistles has become the latest retailer to be targeted by cyber criminals.
items.body:
Hobbs and Phase Eight owner hit by a cyber attack after H&M fears it was targeted
The parent company of fashion brands including Hobbs, Phase Eight and Whistles has become the latest retailer targeted by cyber criminals - as H&M investigates a suspected incident.
South African retail group The Foschini Group (TFG) said it had become aware of a 'cybersecurity incident' on Sunday, affecting its subsidiary TFG London.
It said it had identified the attack, which affected some of its IT systems, on October 11 and had engaged external experts.
‘Our investigation is ongoing and we are working hard to get all our systems back up and running as quickly and safely as we can,’ it said in an email to customers.
TFG London said there was no reason to believe customers’ payment information was at risk, although orders made on or after Sunday may be delayed. Its stores are open as normal.
It comes after H&M said it was investigating claims it was targeted in a cyber attack last week.
The Swedish fashion powerhouse said it is looking into a potential incident made by a group called Shinyhunters, which has previously claimed it was behind the attack on Jaguar Land Rover.
TFG London, which owns Hobbs (pictured), has been targeted by cyber criminals
‘Based on our investigation so far, we have no reason to believe that payment information is at risk. As our investigation continues, we will be working to identify if any sensitive information related to our customers was impacted,’ it said.
‘If we determine that your personal information was affected, you will be directly informed. We do not believe it is necessary to change your account login information at this time.
‘Our investigation is ongoing, and our teams are working tirelessly to get all our systems running again safely.
‘We know this news may be unsettling, and we’re committed to keeping you updated as we have more information to share. We are very sorry for any inconvenience this incident has caused.’
It follows an attack on Asos last week, which saw hackers directly communicate with customers via an app notification.
Messages sent by the hackers to customers' phones said they had 'fully compromised the Snowflake instance', referring to the online platform that collects data, including that of customers.
The retailer confirmed the ‘basic contact details’ of users had been taken in the security breach but said it did not believe payment card details or passwords were affected.
Asos said an 'unauthorised party' gained access by impersonating a trusted contact to get log-in information.
It is now believed that the cyber criminals could have access to more information than Asos originally confirmed. Names, addresses, phone numbers, email addresses and past searches could all have been breached, the BBC reported.

items.title: Extensions and loft conversions plummet as higher costs crush home improvement dreams
items.summary: Extensions and loft conversions are in sharp decline as the cost is too much for homeowners to bear, planning application data shows.
items.body:
Extensions and loft conversions plummet as higher costs crush home improvement dreams
Extensions and loft conversions are in sharp decline as the cost is too much for homeowners to bear, data shows.
Planning applications for two-storey extensions fell by 45 per cent in the four years between 2021 and 2025, according to planning data platform Planning Lens.
Meanwhile, single-storey extensions are down 43 per cent and loft conversions down 40 per cent.
The figures come from the public planning registers of the 77 English councils which have complete records for every year from 2020 to 2025.
Across the 77 councils analysed, there were 47,879 single storey extension applications in 2021. In 2025, that number was 27,478.
Double storey extensions fell from 18,592 in 2021 to 10,147 in 2025 with applications falling in 74 of the 77 councils reviewed. The typical council saw a 47 per cent drop-off in applications.
Expensive business: The costs of extending a home have soared in recent years
Some of this may be attributed to the short-term impact of Covid, where people were keen to improve their homes because they spent more time in them.
However, the figures also showed a significant drop-off in extensions compared to 2019, prior to the pandemic.
Of the 77 councils studied, 48 had records going back to 2018. These figures showed that single-storey applications were 30 per cent lower in 2025 than in 2019.
In terms of double-storey extensions, applications in 2025 were 36 per cent below pre-pandemic levels.
The steepest falls were in Newark and Sherwood in Nottinghamshire, where double storey planning applications were down 68 per cent, as well as the Isle of Wight and Gateshead.
Loft conversions have seen a smaller 17 per cent drop off in the same 48 councils with enough loft applications to compare.
Mark Broome, founder of PlanningLens, said: 'Far fewer people are applying to extend their homes than before the pandemic, and the fall shows no sign of reversing.'
Why aren't people converting their lofts or extending?
Higher mortgage rates are likely a major factor in the slowdown in planning applications, as well as a surge in the cost of building work.
Some homeowners take a further advance from their lender or remortgage their property for a larger amount, in order to release equity to fund renovations - but with mortgage rates higher, doing so can be far more expensive.
In 2021, the lowest rates were 1 per cent. Today they are around 5 per cent.

|---|---|---|---|
| 2018 | 8,184 | 17,770 | 2,345 |

| 2024 | 5,501 | 13,751 | 2,958 |

| Source: PlanningLens |  |  |  | 
Adding an extra £100,000 to the mortgage, to be paid off over 20 years now costs £660 a month compared to £460 a month five years ago.
Building materials are now 39 per cent higher than they were pre-pandemic, according to tradesperson directory MyBuilder.
There has also been a surge in labour costs, which now amount to up to 55 per cent of total costs for extensions and renovations.
James Perris, managing director at De Villiers surveyors, says: 'Where we used to allow £25,000 for a loft conversion, that is now £50,000, where you could get a tradesman for £150 a day that is now £300 and that is mainly since 2020.
'Secondly, we are also suffering from a reduced European workforce since Brexit and thirdly much higher borrowing costs - so generally people can’t afford to do the work.
'Unfortunately it has also created a rise in sub standard workmanship where people are going for the lowest price without realising that they may be employing inexperienced tradesmen.'
Andy Simms, building expert at MyBuilder, adds: 'The covid pandemic was a big factor.
'Home improvement demands surged once it ended, and this, alongside Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, led to a spike in the cost of raw materials.
'Labour is now the biggest deciding cost factor. While materials themselves did not go up last year, labour costs actually rose by 7 per cent in the same timeframe, and continue to do so.'
Another issue is the fact many can't find a tradesperson to begin with.
Simms adds: 'It’s reported that there is a notable shortage of workers within the construction industry, with an extra 47,860 workers per year needed to meet necessary demands.
'The shortage of skilled labour has been a real worry for millions of UK homeowners, with our data finding that 33 per cent of Britons have recently struggled to find an available tradesperson.'

items.body:
Kingfisher raids European home improvement retailer OBI to bring in Sebastian Gundel as its new CEO
Kingfisher, which owns B&Q and Screwfix in the UK and Castorama and Brico Depot in France and other markets, has announced the appointment of Sebastian Gundel as Chief Executive Officer, effective 1st February 2027. He will join Kingfisher’s board of directors on the same date.
He brings more than two decades of leadership experience in the home improvement sector, including as Chief Executive Officer at European retailer OBI, where he led the company's evolution from traditional retail to a digitally enabled, customer centric, omnichannel business.
Prior to becoming CEO, he served as Chief Customer & Digital Officer, leading OBI's omnichannel transformation and digital innovation agenda. His responsibilities spanned loyalty, marketplaces and ecosystem development, as well as the expansion of trade propositions.
Claudia Arney, Chair, says: “Following a thorough selection process, the board is delighted to appoint Sebastian as Chief Executive Officer. Sebastian combines deep experience in home improvement retail and clear expertise in Kingfisher’s strategic growth drivers with a strong track record of innovation and operational delivery. He will build on the significant progress made under Thierry Garnier’s leadership while bringing fresh perspectives as we continue to evolve the business. Sebastian has the board’s full support as he leads Kingfisher through its next phase of growth and value creation.”
Gundel says: “It is a privilege to be appointed Chief Executive Officer of Kingfisher. I have long admired the strength and diversity of Kingfisher’s retail banners, its scale and its strategic ambition. The industry is evolving rapidly, creating significant opportunities across trade, digital, marketplaces, services and new customer propositions. I am much looking forward to working with the team to build on those opportunities and create sustainable long-term value.”
Garnier will remain in role until 31st December, when he will step down as CEO and board member. Bhavesh Mistry, CFO, will serve as interim CEO during the month of January. Arney will continue as Chair until the company's 2029 annual general meeting.
Garnier says: “It has been an honour to lead Kingfisher, and I am proud of what our teams have achieved together. Sebastian brings deep sector expertise, a strong customer focus and a proven track record of performance. I am confident that he will successfully lead Kingfisher through its next chapter.”
Morrisons
Morrisons recently appointed Dr Mohsen Ghasempour as Chief AI Officer, a newly created role that will see him establish a central data science and AI function for the UK grocery retailer. He joined from Kingfisher, where he had served as Chief AI Officer since March 2024 following more than two years as Group AI Director.
He will take overall responsibility for data and AI strategy, with a remit spanning customer growth, colleague empowerment, operational efficiency, manufacturing excellence and commercial excellence. He will report directly to Morrisons CEO Rami Baitiéh when he takes up the role on 1st October.
“Creation of this new role reflects our commitment to ensuring Morrisons is embracing the opportunities in data and AI at pace, with focus and in the right way,” said Baitiéh.
“Mohsen is a recognised expert in the field with hands on experience of unlocking the potential of technology to deliver innovative new solutions that serve customers, empower colleagues and deliver measurable business impact.”
Ghasempour said: “I’m excited about joining Morrisons and building the team that will help the business make effective and responsible use of AI in the years ahead, to deliver real benefits for customers and colleagues.”

items.title: Cost of living struggles inspire 'social supermarket'
items.summary: New social supermarket offers cheaper groceries with dignity and choice.
items.body:
Cost of living struggles inspire 'social supermarket'
- Published
"Instead of going to a food bank, being handed a bag and getting back home then finding out that they won't use all those items, at least here they can buy the tokens and shop around for the items they would choose to buy."
Founder Thomas Cliffe hopes the first "social supermarket" in Newcastle-under-Lyme, designed to help people struggling with the cost of living, will offer the "freedom to shop with dignity".
Set up by Community Cupboard NUL CIC, the store allows members to buy groceries at cost price or below, with more choice than other outlets.
Customers can sign up for a membership costing Â£1 for 12 months. They are then able to purchase tokens to spend on items throughout the store.
Cliffe said the idea was inspired by his own experience after leaving work because of anxiety.
Although his wife was still employed, he said the couple struggled financially and found they were unable to access some forms of support.
"It was horrible because you start to panic and think: 'What am I supposed to do? Where am I going to get the next food from?'"
"We either had to choose a meal or choose the bills."
The supermarket opened for the first time on Monday.
Such stores aim to cut food waste while helping people facing food insecurity by selling surplus goods at lower prices.
"It was exciting to have everyone come through the doors for the first time and give them that freedom to shop with dignity," Cliffe said.
Voluntary co-director Laura Steele said the level of need in the area often went unnoticed.
"One in four children experience poverty from what we have found, and the average income is Â£29,000."
"There was nothing really for the people of Newcastle and it was crying out for it really," she said.
Cheryl Pepper, a carer who visited after finishing a night shift, described the supermarket as "absolutely brilliant".
"The food's cheap. If you go to Tesco you spend Â£100, but you come in here, I've put Â£20 on and I still have some tokens left," she said.
Recent research on the growth of social supermarkets, external backed the idea that they were less off-putting than food banks and large commercial stores for those facing food insecurity.
But lead researcher, Dr Claire O'Malley from Teesside University, said: "While social supermarkets can improve access to affordable food and reduce waste in the short term, they should not be viewed as a complete solution to food insecurity."
The report called for them to supplement, rather than replace, government support for those struggling to put good food on the table.
Fiona Morris, who has ADHD, said she had often found large supermarkets overwhelming.
After visiting the new store, she said she immediately felt understood by staff.
"It feels like Supermarket Sweep - I feel like I'm robbing the place," she said.

items.body:
UK grocery retailer Morrisons notches up Too Good To Go surplus food mobile app milestone
Morrisons reports a milestone in its Too Good To Go surplus food partnership. In a LinkedIn post, Rami Baitiéh, CEO at Morrisons, said: “Every second, 80,000 meals go to waste globally. It's a statistic that should make everyone in the food industry pause.”
“When you face numbers of that scale, it is easy to feel that individual action doesn't matter. But at Morrisons, we believe the best way to drive real change is by making it simple, affordable, and rewarding for our customers to make a difference. That is why I'm incredibly proud to share that we have officially saved 4,000,000 meals from going to waste since our partnership with Too Good To Go began in 2019.”
He added: “For those who haven't used it, Too Good To Go is an app that connects people with surplus, unsold food before it gets thrown away. By offering Morrisons Surprise Bags on the app at less than half price, we are ensuring perfectly good, fresh food stays out of the bin while helping households enjoy high quality groceries at a fraction of the cost.”
“Last month, we welcomed Chelsea Kerr from Too Good To Go to our internal event, Teamtalk, and together we celebrated this massive milestone. Behind this achievement is the amazing effort from our colleagues who pack these bags daily, and our customers who step up to rescue them. A huge thank you to everyone involved. To continue this great work, we'll be bringing our new Chilled Surprise Bags, which we're trialing in 25 London stores, to the rest of our supermarkets in the coming months - watch this space!”
M&S
Over 350 M&S Food stores now offer Too Good To Go Surprise Bags made up of surplus bakery products, giving customers the chance to collect food at a reduced price at the end of the day directly from in-store bakeries.
The national launch follows a trial in a select number of locations across the UK and is the latest move in M&S Food’s work to reduce food waste and ensure good food doesn’t go to waste. The Surprise Bags will include the likes of pastries, cookies and bread baked in-store. Each will include three to four products to a minimum retail price of £10.20 for £3.80. Customers can order them through the aforementioned app and collect them Monday to Saturday, one hour before their local store closes.
The partnership sits alongside M&S’s wider Plan A programme to halve food waste by 2030 and to help edible surplus food find its way to a dinner plate.
Lucinda Langton, Head of Sustainability at M&S Food, says: “Too Good To Go is a brilliant example of how we’re turning our commitment to reducing food waste into practical action. By giving customers access to surprise bags of surplus bakery products, we can help ensure more of our food is enjoyed. The response from our trial stores has been outstanding, and this partnership is another positive step towards our goal of halving food waste by 2030.”
Chelsea Kerr, Managing Director at Too Good To Go UK & Ireland, says: “We’re delighted to be partnering with M&S to help make their surplus food available to even more customers across the UK and Ireland. Food waste is a huge challenge, but partnerships like this show how simple it can be for businesses and consumers to take action together.”
“By giving food that might otherwise go unsold another chance to be enjoyed, we’re making it easier for people to save good food while also getting great value. M&S is a much loved brand across the UK, so we’re excited to be working together to make saving food from going to waste a simple and accessible part of everyday life for even more people.”

2026 RTIH Innovation Awards RFID Project of the Year finalists include Checkpoint Systems and RADAR
We’re pleased to announce the shortlist for the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards RFID Project of the Year category. We received a record number of entries this year and many fantastic examples of technology excellence driving transformative change across the global retail sector.
Check out a rundown of our 2026 shortlists and finalists here.
Congratulations to all those who made it through the initial submission process! It’s now over to our star studded judging panel who will decide the winners to be announced at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony, taking place at The HAC in Central London.
The event will be held on Wednesday, 4th November and consist of a drinks reception, three course meal, awards ceremony presided over by award winning stand-up comedian, presenter, actor and broadcaster, Aurie Styla, and after party until 1am.
Click here to book your place at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony on Wednesday, 4th November.
Our 2026 RFID Project of the Year finalists as follows:
Checkpoint Systems and JD Sports
JD Sports is transforming inventory management across its European estate using RFID technology. Following a 2024 pilot with Checkpoint Systems, RFID was deployed to over 400 UK and Ireland stores during 2025, with the remaining 680 European stores targeted by October 2026.
Checkpoint’s ItemOptix software provides them with real-time inventory visibility, improving stock accuracy, shelf replenishment and product availability while enabling more advanced, data-driven retail operations for the future. RFID is also being extended across JD Sports’ European distribution centres, combining ItemOptix software with RFID tunnel technology to improve inventory visibility throughout their supply chain.
Edgbaston and Levy
The Edgbaston RFID Smart Cup System transformed the management of reusable cups during the 2026 cricket season. Replacing a legacy deposit refund process with RFID enabled cup validation, the solution ensured deposits could only be refunded when a genuine deposit backed cup was scanned.
Alongside improving financial controls, the system enhanced cup return performance, reduced cup losses, lowered staffing requirements and delivered a more efficient returns operation across major sporting events. The project combined RFID technology, automated validation and operational process redesign to create a scalable circular economy solution. Across the first full season, the system achieved a 95.7% cup return rate, improved deposit integrity and generated significant labour and security savings, demonstrating both commercial and sustainability benefits.
Lager 157 and ClarityRFID
Lager 157, a Swedish fashion retailer, has partnered with ClarityRFID to pilot the Clarity Store solution across three stores in Denmark, Sweden and Finland.
Over three months, the pilot replaced manual stock counting and shipment receiving with real-time, item level RFID data, lifting stock accuracy to as high as 98-99.8% and SKU accuracy to as high as 97% in participating stores.
For a retailer built on product, price and word of mouth trust rather than traditional marketing, that level of inventory visibility strengthens the promise at the centre of the brand: knowing exactly what's in stock, in which size and colour, at which store. Lager 157 and ClarityRFID are now working toward a full production roll-out across the retailer's six-country store network, planned for 2027.
RADAR
RADAR lays claim to being the only vertically integrated provider of overhead RFID, delivering perpetual, item level inventory intelligence for retail at scale.
Through item detection and location sensing today, and expanding user behavior analytics over time, RADAR gives retailers the ability to measure their physical stores the way they already measure their ecommerce business, turning one accurate inventory foundation into a different advantage for every function of the business.
As of Q3 2026, RADAR is deployed across more than 1,700 stores and 21 million square feet of retail space, indexing over 55 million products and processing more than 130 billion tag reads daily.

2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Retail Media Technology finalists include Hanshow, Jisp, and Lloyds
We’re pleased to announce the shortlist for the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Retail Media Technology category. We received a record number of entries this year and many fantastic examples of technology excellence driving transformative change across the global retail sector.
Check out a rundown of our 2026 shortlists and finalists here.
Congratulations to all those who made it through the initial submission process! It’s now over to our star studded judging panel who will decide the winners to be announced at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony, taking place at The HAC in Central London.
The event will be held on Wednesday, 4th November and consist of a drinks reception, three course meal, awards ceremony presided over by award winning stand-up comedian, presenter, actor and broadcaster, Aurie Styla, and after party until 1am.
Click here to book your place at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony on Wednesday, 4th November.
Our 2026 Retail Media Innovation finalists as follows:
Age-Gate by Adello
Age-Gate by Adello places a camera-based age check inside a mobile ad unit, so age restricted advertising is shown only after the viewer's age has been checked.
The facial age estimate runs on the user's own device, and no image is stored or transferred. In a two-week live campaign in Switzerland's tobacco category in May 2026, using a deliberately generic creative, the unit delivered 67,801 impressions at 63.5% viewability and 1.1 minutes average dwell time. 25.6% of users who engaged completed the age check. Switzerland's revised tobacco law, expected in early 2027, requires age controls for online tobacco advertising.
FashSYNC
FashSYNC is an in-store retail media platform delivering real-time SKU level intent detection and closed loop attribution on Samsung digital out-of-home (DOOH) displays. It is unlocking a $22-30 billion untapped retail media market in premium fashion, where grocery retail media dominates (Cooler Screens) but fashion has remained fragmented and undermonetised.
Hanshow
Hanshow, shopreme and Lucky Cart have created a unified smart cart ecosystem that brings personalised, measurable retail media into the physical shopping journey. Hanshow provides the connected hardware and in-store technology foundation, shopreme delivers the smart cart software, self-scanning experience and store integration, while Lucky Cart contributes its personalisation and retail media capabilities.
Together, the solution transforms the shopping cart into an intelligent touchpoint supporting product discovery, relevant offers, basket visibility and faster checkout. Already deployed with a leading European grocery retailer, it demonstrates how physical stores can combine digital convenience, shopper first engagement and new retail media opportunities through one scalable platform.
Jisp
Jisp's Scan & Win Video platform turned McVitie's Moments packaging into an always on shopper engagement channel for long-standing FMCG partner Pladis.
Using Scan & Win’s new video technology to allow the scanning of a physical product to start entry (not on-pack QR), instant win mechanics and multi-channel marketing, the six-week campaign generated over 1,000 product scans from 132 unique shoppers, with 62% returning to scan more than once, a new benchmark for the platform.
Paid social reached over 137,000 consumers at a 3% click-through rate, while owned channels drove more than 5,400 landing page visits. Beyond engagement, the campaign delivered valuable first-party shopper data for Pladis.
Lloyds Rewards
Lloyds Rewards is one of the UK's largest bank led retail media platforms. Connecting over ten million eligible customers with retailers, brands and partner propositions through Lloyds' digital channels. Over the past year, Lloyds has evolved Rewards beyond traditional cashback, introducing challenges, prize draws, retailer discounts and strategic partnerships to create multiple ways for brands to engage customers.
Particular Audience and Intersport Austria
Particular Audience and Intersport Austria have put relevance at the centre of on-site retail media. Instead of letting bids alone decide what shoppers see, Particular Audience's AI ranks sponsored and organic results together, so ads stay useful to the shopper.
In the first five weeks the programme delivered 536,653 impressions, 6,988 clicks and a 1.30% click-through rate at a 17.2% cost of sale. Brand halo ROAS reached 17.3x against 5.81x on SKU last click, McKINLEY and Active Rebel brand sales rose 28.6% and 28.5%, and a Bayesian A/B test showed a 100% probability of beating control.

items.title: Budget is a 'critical test' for John Healey as high street grapples with rising costs and 'fragile' confidence
items.summary: With John Healey facing crunch talks with industry bosses on Downing Street this morning, the British Retail Consortium (BRC) warned further tax hikes would push up prices and cost jobs.
items.body:
Budget is a 'critical test' for John Healey as high street grapples with rising costs and 'fragile' confidence
The Chancellor has been warned he faces a 'critical test' in the Budget as the High Street grapples with rising costs and 'fragile' confidence.
With John Healey facing crunch talks with industry bosses on Downing Street this morning, the British Retail Consortium (BRC) warned further tax hikes would push up prices and cost jobs.
And it said retail sales rose by just 1.3 per cent in the year to September - far slower than the 2.3 per cent increase seen 12 months earlier.
'The Chancellor cannot promise to ease the cost of living while piling more costs onto the retailers working to keep prices down,' said BRC chief executive Helen Dickinson.
'With confidence fragile, this Budget is a critical test. Retailers will do everything they can to protect value for customers, but Government must play its part.
'Another rise in business rates would push up pressure on prices, choke off high-street investment and put local jobs at risk.
Retailers have urged the Chancellor not to pile the sector with further tax rises at the Budget
'This Budget must back retail to invest, employ and grow - not make it harder.'
The comments came after Marks & Spencer chief executive Stuart Machin urged Healey to 'to get Britain growing again by taking the handcuffs off business' in the Budget on October 28.
Writing in the Daily Mail on Saturday, Machin branded Labour's previous two efforts under Rachel Reeves 'a disaster' and said: 'At the very least, he should start unravelling the mistakes of the last two Budgets.'
The Chancellor will hold talks with retail and hospitality chiefs at 11 Downing Street today.
Representatives from businesses and trade groups including the Co-op, the British Beauty Council and UK Hospitality are expected at the breakfast meeting.
Retailers have cited the high cost of employment - related to inflation-busting rises in the minimum wage and a surprise increase to National insurance contributions for firms - as a major headache.
The war in the Middle East has also driven up the costs such as ingredients and energy.
Large retailers have been particularly concerned that Andy Burnham's promise to cut business rates for pubs, clubs and music venues will be funded by hitting supermarkets with a so-called 'warehouse tax'.
But it was reported over the weekend that this was not in Healey's plans for the Budget.
Small businesses are also calling for help, however, with industry groups calling for thousands of firms to be excluded from paying business rates altogether.
The Federation of Small Businesses (FSB) said raising a key threshold that gives firms business rates relief from £12,000 to £25,000 would help unlock growth by removing 250,000 small firms from the levy.
Tina McKenzie, FSB's national chairman, said: 'Small businesses across the UK are up against huge and persistent cost rises that are seeing so many struggle with running their business, let alone investing and expanding. This is the most important opportunity for the Government to make its more pro-small business tone a reality.
'If we are to get the growth needed, the Budget must be a moment for some meaningful action, backing the small firms and self employed that are so crucial to the economy.
'We need a tax system that rewards ambition rather than punishes it.'

items.body:
Tech for Retail 2026 preview: retail leaders and technology innovators set to meet in Paris
Tech for Retail will return to Paris on 30th November and 1st December, bringing together more than 420 exhibitors, 15,000 retail decision-makers and over 200 conferences at Paris Expo Porte de Versailles. For its sixth edition, the European retail technology show will place artificial intelligence, omnichannel commerce, supply chain transformation, data and the augmented store at the heart of its programme.
A strong international line-up will complement a French retail perspective, with senior executives from across Europe and global retail organisations taking to the Main Stage.
AI, innovation and the future of retail
The event will open on 30th November with Alexandre Bompard, Chairman and CEO at Carrefour, setting the tone for two days focused on the technologies reshaping the retail industry. He will be followed by Delphine Viguier-Hovasse, L’Oréal’s Chief Innovation & Prospective Officer, Artefact CEO and founder Vincent Luciani, and Bernard Osta, CEO at second-hand fashion marketplace Vestiaire Collective.
AI will be a recurring theme throughout the programme, moving beyond experimentation towards practical applications across retail operations, customer experience and commerce. Sessions will explore how technology can deliver measurable impact, from product data and personalisation to new approaches to customer engagement.
The luxury and beauty sectors will also feature prominently. A dedicated session, The Reinvention of Luxury through Technology, will bring together Nathalie Cabut from L’Oréal, Elise Ducret from Carita and Pascale Miguet from Publicis Luxe to discuss how technology is changing the luxury experience.
A truly European perspective
International speakers will bring a broader perspective to the conversations around retail transformation.
On 1st December, Mikko Kärkkäinen, Group CEO and Co-Founder at Finnish retail technology company RELEX Solutions, will open the second day with a keynote focused on supply chain and logistics. His appearance reflects the growing importance of technology in forecasting, planning and building more agile retail operations.
The programme will also feature Nadine Graf, President Europe, UK & Ireland & Emerging Markets at The Estée Lauder Companies, and Michelle Lamberti, Chief Omnicommerce Officer at ADEO. Their sessions will add an international dimension to discussions around beauty, customer journeys and the convergence of physical and digital commerce.
Food retail will have a strong presence too. Martín Tolcachir, CEO at Grupo DIA, Fredy El Hakim, IT Procurement Manager at Mercadona, and Nacho Gonzalez Hernandez, CEO and Board Member at Spanish retail association AECOC, will discuss how technology can move from innovation to practical, scalable impact.
From the augmented store to sustainable retail
The programme will look beyond AI alone, reflecting the increasingly interconnected challenges facing retailers. A session on the augmented store will examine the balance between retail media, digitalisation and energy efficiency, with Miguel Ángel González Gisbert from Carrefour, Sébastien Fourcy from Vusion and Marc Taieb from Wifirst. Other sessions will address sustainability, circular economy, regulation, recommerce and new revenue models.
The show will also explore the evolution of product data as a strategic asset, the role of AI in content and merchandising, and the impact of technology on European marketplaces and omnichannel strategies.
Alongside the conference programme, Tech for Retail will offer visitors access to more than 420 exhibitors and 75+ startups, as well as thematic guided tours designed to help retailers identify relevant technologies and solutions. The event will also host Innovation, AI, Customer Experience and Startup Awards, highlighting technologies and companies shaping the next phase of retail.
With senior retail executives, technology providers and international speakers gathered under one roof, Tech for Retail 2026 will offer a European view of how technology is moving from experimentation to implementation, and how retailers can turn innovation into tangible business value.

“Your product page is your new home page,” when it comes to discovery in the agentic AI era, said Philip Hall, MD, Europe at Rithum, during FT Live 2026: Future of Retail in London last week. Fellow conference session panellists from L’Oréal and Wolf & Badger, a marketplace that champions independent fashion and homeware, emphasised how important good data tagging, quality, and hygiene is amid a digital revolution where AI agents can buy on behalf of consumers.
According to Matt Berzinski, EMEA Field CTO at Ping Identity, who was also on the panel entitled ‘The new online storefront - unlocking the next phase of agentic commerce’ on 6th October: “AI agents are inherently lazy, so if you’re too hard to find they will just move on.” Having good data mastery is therefore more important than it has ever been.
“It is also up to us to identify agents and control them,” he added, as the conference session panel moved on to discuss the centrality of good governance and know your agent (KYA) compliance. This could become as vital as customer (KYC) compliance requirements in the future. “Trust is crucial in this coming era where the ability to know who is a human, who is an agent, and to have appropriate verification is key.”
GEO
Aside from security internally and with ecosystem partners, data mastery is also vital for the Generative Engine Optimisation (GEO) future that will displace traditional SEO in search in the future. The skill of structuring and tailoring online content so that AI large language models (LLMs), such as ChatGPT and Gemini, can find and recommend your brand will be crucial in driving future sales.
As Othman Bennis, Chief Digital and Marketing Officer, L’Oréal Europe, said: “L’Oréal is moving to having 18-20 data fields to hundreds in the future in terms of our product attributes. This is necessary for the agentic AI future.” He also shared that his firm is working with OpenAI now that they’ve opened an ad function on ChatGPT.
Early days
George Graham, CEO at Wolf & Badger, noted that his firm was the first in Europe to take an agentic AI initiated order. “We are already transacting,” he said, while stressing it is very early days in the migration to agentic commerce. “We use Stripe’s agentic commerce suite of tools and work with Meta to enable our offering.”
Pricing pressure
In regard to the potential pricing pressure from AI agents searching out better deals for their humans, using economies-of-scale negotiating tactics depending on their number of adherents, Rithum’s Hall thought this likely. “LLMs will tend to direct you to the cheapest price. However, I personally don’t just shop on price, so there is still room for retailers to differentiate themselves.”
According to Wolf & Badger’s Graham fundamentally they’re still a retailer that needs to curate their offering to achieve the best products on their platform, the best service, loyalty and retention, at the best price they can get. This means delivering: Good CX; Products, price and service; Fulfilment. “These are always at the core of good retailing,” he said. “The fundamentals don’t change.”
L’Oréal Europe’s Bennis agreed, although he did stress his company is not complacent about the coming revolution and is already working with Alibaba and Amazon among others to protect discoverability. “Ultimately though, it is the one with the best CX that will win this race.”
There is no doubting that the race is underway. “Don’t leave too many data gaps and you’ll be OK,” he reassured attendees, while stressing that if you do then the agent might get it wrong when classifying your brand. “Don’t give them the chance. Don’t put your brand out there with a terrible dataset.”
It appears that data really is the ‘new oil’ in the coming agentic AI era where it will grease the modern economy in the way petrol did the 20th century. Retailers need to be ready for the coming revolution.
Q&A
In response to questioning from RTIH, the participants said they weren’t worried about the possibility of AI agents sifting through data that had already been sifted by other agents.
The virgin internet, where human checked and verified information can be mined and interrogated, is fast becoming a thing of the past. But this wasn’t a worry to the panellists, or at least it’s outside of their control and parameters. Verification against inaccuracies or fakes is also a potential countermeasure.
“Even if you’re training on synthetic data that has been artificially created, retailers will still have their own data control mechanisms and procedures,” said Wolf & Badger’s Graham. Rithum’s Hall, meanwhile, advised retailers in the room to just concentrate on what they can control and to get that right.

Ikea flagship store brings home furnishing products to Douyin E-commerce shoppers across China
Ingka Group has launched an Ikea Douyin official flagship store in China. The new digital touchpoint will offer more than 6,500 Ikea products across 179 categories, with delivery available in 301 cities across China.
The move brings the retailer in to the short-form video and content commerce platform (a sister platform to TikTok under ByteDance). The store will complement its existing stores, website, app, WeChat and other e-commerce channels in China.

Douyin E-commerce gives us an opportunity to meet people in a new context, learn what resonates with them and make Ikea more accessible to more people. This is not simply about adding another sales channel. It is about understanding how we can become part of people’s everyday lives in new and relevant ways.”
