items.body:
2026 RTIH Innovation Awards finalists assemble! Presenting this week's biggest retail technology stories
It's Friday, the weekend is almost upon us, so let’s kick back and reflect on another eventful week for the retail tech space. Here's your briefing on the most important stories from the past few days, including Lidl GB, Deliveroo, Walmart, OpenAI, Morrisons, StrongPoint ALS, VoCoVo, The Very Group, Jysk, Enactor, Zalando, Asda, and Rokt.
1. Lidl deploys new self-checkouts that show UK shoppers on screens across retailer's store network
Lidl is rolling out new self-checkouts across its UK stores which play video footage back to customers while they are scanning their shopping. These will be deployed in all new stores and retrofitted into existing locations.
They will feature built in overhead cameras, vertically mounted large format screens, and LED lights to alert staff if people need help while scanning their shopping. To leave, customers must scan a receipt printed by the machine at a gate at the exit.
Roll-out is also taking place across hundreds of Lidl and Kaufland stores in Germany.
A Lidl spokesperson told RTIH: “The new self-checkouts are designed to be more customer friendly, enhancing the shopping experience while boosting efficiency.”
2. Morrisons partners with StrongPoint ALS and VoCoVo on Click & Collect pilot at Skipton store
Morrisons has launched a pilot of StrongPoint ALS’s temperature controlled Click & Collect lockers at the retailer’s Skipton store in North Yorkshire.
The aim here is to provide a convenient and flexible way to collect ambient, chilled and frozen groceries.
In a LinkedIn post, Christopher Evison, Senior Productivity Manager at Morrisons, said: “This is a great step forward for Click & Collect at Morrisons. It brings faster pickups - orders are pre-packed in paper bags and loaded into the lockers in advance. Simply enter your unique six-digit code when you arrive and go. And more flexibility - the lockers are helping us extend operating hours by two hours a day, giving customers even more options for when they collect. Freshness is guaranteed - the multi-temperature lockers can accommodate ambient, chilled and frozen products, whether customers are picking up a few essentials or their full weekly shop.”
He added: “There is also support when you need it - integrated VoCoVo headsets provide a direct two-way connection to store colleagues, making it easy to get assistance or complete any required ID checks. Huge thank you to all that have supported from both StrongPoint and Vocovo. It’s another great step forward in investing in our online proposition while keeping customer convenience at the heart of what we do. A huge well done to everyone involved in getting the launch over the line - a fantastic team effort. We’re really looking forward to seeing customers using the lockers and continuing to drive our online propostion forward.”
3. Walmart joins OpenAI's ChatGPT fashion push as Virtual Try On and Favourites launch
A dress spotted on social media, an outfit for an autumn wedding or a new style to try: OpenAI is adding tools to ChatGPT that let shoppers move from an idea to an image of themselves wearing it, with Walmart among the retailers involved from launch.
The new Virtual Try On and Favourites features allow users to visualise clothing and accessories using their own photographs, then save products to return to later. Shoppers can describe what they want, upload an image of an item or use a screenshot as the starting point for a search.
Walmart is bringing its fashion range into the experience. Daniel Danker, EVP AI Acceleration, Product, and Design, said on LinkedIn that the US retail giant was working with OpenAI “from day one” to make its fashion available through Virtual Try On, Shop this Look and Favourites.
Sharing an example himself, he added: “Found something I like. Think I should I buy it?”
4. Deliveroo teams with Coco on launch of food and grocery on demand delivery robots in some parts of UK
Deliveroo is gearing up to roll-out delivery robots, supplied by US company Coco, in the UK. These will be used for takeaways and groceries, with Deliveroo claiming that the robots will not replace human riders but rather complement them during off peak hours.
Canary Wharf, Milton Keynes, Leeds, Stockton-on-Tees, and Nottingham are the initial areas to get the service, with plans afoot for a broader UK roll-out.
Deliveroo runs a three-sided marketplace across roughly restaurants, grocers and retailers, all promising delivery in as little as 30 minutes. It is also a DoorDash subsidiary now, after being taken over by the US giant in a deal valuing the business at £2.9 billion. So this move shouldn’t come as a huge surprise.
5. The Very Group teams with AI powered e-commerce personalisation platform Made With Intent
The Very Group, which operates digital retailers Very and Littlewoods, has partnered with Made With Intent. By using over 800 behavioural signals, Made With Intent’s agentic decision engine predicts customer’s intent in real-time, helping to decide what they see and when.
Very says it will now be able to spotlight discount offers unique to customers based on individual shopping trends, as well as provide prompts at crucial moments throughout the shopping experience. Made With Intent’s engine is built on a proprietary model and optimisation AI agent that work together to allocate experiences across hundreds of intent combinations, learning what works for which visitors and contexts then applying it to future sessions.
Sarah Hanna, Digital Director at The Very Group, comments: “Made With Intent’s agentic platform unlocks fast paced, scalable real-time personalisation that can be executed to help enhance the customer experience, ultimately influencing our commercial KPIs. In fact, in the first month of the partnership, we’ve already seen promising results including revenue per customer increasing by a fifth in one of our agentic strategies, and an uplift in overall conversion.”
“Made With Intent gives our e-commerce team a brand new lever that they can effortlessly activate to make a difference on what our customers see and when, whether that’s one-off discounts or personalised payment options. It’s all about giving customers the right experience at the right time.”
6. John Lewis, Asda, Morrisons, H&M, Dunelm, and Waitrose among 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards finalists
We're hugely pleased to present the finalists and shortlists for the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards, sponsored by 3D Cloud, Business France, and Retail Technology Show 2027. We received a record number of entries this year and many fantastic examples of technology excellence driving transformative change across the global retail sector
Congratulations to all those who made it through the initial submission process! It’s now over to our star studded judging panel who will decide the winners to be announced at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony, taking place at The HAC in Central London.
The event will be held on Wednesday, 4th November and consist of a drinks reception, three course meal, awards ceremony presided over by award winning stand-up comedian, presenter, actor and broadcaster, Aurie Styla, and after party until 1am.
Click here to book your place at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony on Wednesday, 4th November.
7. Ceva Logistics taps Sereact AI robotic systems for Zalando returns handling in Germany and Poland
Sereact, Zalando and CEVA Logistics have announced the launch of AI powered automated returns processing across key fulfillment facilities in Germany (Greven) and Poland (Świebodzin). Powered by Cortex, Sereact’s physical AI platform, the dual-arm robotic systems have entered live operations to autonomously process returned fashion items, marking the initial phase of a broader initiative to scale returns automation across Europe.
Cortex groups previously unseen objects - identifying, grasping and sorting items dynamically without requiring article specific training or pre-determined article sets. The technology is designed to work alongside humans. By taking on highly repetitive handling, it aims to reduce physical strain on employees, allowing them to move into higher value roles where human expertise and judgement are required.
“At the heart of our collaboration with Sereact and CEVA is a fundamental belief: true innovation happens when technology and human potential advance together. By solving the most complex challenges in modern fulfilment today, we are actively shaping the future of e-commerce logistics for fashion and lifestyle,” says Masood Choudhry, SVP Logistics at Zalando, which in July joined Sereact’s Series B round as an investor.
8. Currys ramps up social activity as it goes live on TikTok Shop
Currys has launched on TikTok Shop with a curated range of products, from health and beauty and coffee to seasonal and audio.
Building on the retailer’s TikTok activity, with its page having bagged over ten million ‘likes’, it will partner with content creators to showcase products to new audiences, and will host TikTok Live shopping events, bringing real-time product demos and instant purchasing to customers' feeds.
This will start as a trial in partnership with THG Commerce who will provide strategy, trading, shop management, weekly live streams and affiliate management services. As an official TikTok Shop partner, THG Commerce says it has generated over £44 million in GMV for its partners by providing a complete solution that covers everything from initial storefront setup and compliance to content creation, global fulfilment and customer services, managed under one roof.
9. Asda and Rokt team up to bring AI powered relevant offers to customers at checkout
Asda has partnered with Rokt to deliver relevant offers to the UK grocery retailer’s customers at checkout across its online grocery business and George, its clothing and home brand. Using Rokt Pay+ on the payment page and Rokt Thanks on the order confirmation page, Asda says it has created a new retail media revenue stream at the point of purchase, while customer conversion remains unchanged.
Rokt uses AI to determine the most relevant next action for each customer in real-time on both the payments and confirmation pages.
“Checkout is a critical part of the customer journey, so we were deliberate about how we approached it,” says Chris Chalmers, Vice President Customer Data and Loyalty at Asda “The results show we can make that experience more relevant for customers while creating meaningful new value for the business.”
10. Jysk rolls out Enactor powered unified commerce platform in Norway with Holland and Belgium next
Danish home furnishing retailer Jysk has gone live in Norway with its Enactor powered unified commerce platform. It has spent the last couple of months transitioning all 110 of its stores in the country to the new platform.
This integrates all store systems into one unified solution, with the aim of making everyday processes simpler and more efficient for both colleagues and customers.
“We now have several points of sale throughout the store, which means we can help customers and process payments wherever they are. My team has done an amazing job, and they really love the new way of working. It has been great to see how quickly it has become a natural part of our daily routines,” says Connie Evensen, Store Manager at Jysk Furuset in Oslo.
Sweden and Finland joined the new platform a couple of weeks ago, and the Netherlands and Belgium are up next.

items.body:
FT Live Future of Retail Summit review: store experiences still count says JD Group CEO Régis Schultz
The physical store is still important because “it’s where we connect with consumers”, said Régis Schultz, CEO at JD Group, in a keynote address at the FT Live 2026 Future of Retail event in London this week.
“We’re going for bigger stores with a view to giving customers’ experiences,” explained Schultz, while discussing his company’s in-store cafes, barbers, till checkout service in under a minute, constant stock availability in large units, such as the one at a Westfield shopping centre in London where it effectively has a warehouse in the back-end with attendant technology.
“Humans are social animals. We want to serve that need and give instant gratification - online can never do that,” he said, while adding it isn’t as good for the brand either, although it does of course have its place…The industry used to talk about a seamless omnichannel experience in retail. But no more. It should be different with the store offering an alternative to online.”
Stores still matter
“Offline needs to be more efficient, however, when ‘competing’ with digital options,” he added in a conference session conversation with Laura Onita, Retail Correspondent at the Financial Times (FT). “The 15-20% conversion rate in-store can be better.”
“AI technology can potentially help with that,” he later added when considering better personalisation via greater data mastery; inventory control and constant stock availability; and designing and promoting great store experiences. “We don’t do self-checkout at tills a lot in our stores either because it’s too complex in regard to the security tags for higher value goods…We do have over one billion people per year in traffic at JD, so it’s just a question of right product, at the right price, and getting that experience right in terms of growing the business.”
As part of that great customer experience that he is targeting, the French head of JD Group joked that “even UK consumers don’t like to queue”. However, high labour costs don’t help the firm in terms of meeting its less than one minute queuing time target.
Future threats?
In terms of any threats that Shultz sees on the horizon for his burgeoning global business, youth unemployment is a crucial worry for him, both in terms of how bad it is for youngsters themselves not to have work and to be able to develop, but also in terms of how it adversely impacts their spending power and ultimately his bottom line.
“Youth unemployment is bad in the UK at the moment,” he said. Indeed, the Not in Education, Employment, or Training (NEET) debate is presently very high on the political agenda.
“Europe isn’t good either. The US is better,” he added, while reflecting on his own first job stacking shelves and how important it was in getting him started and motivated. “If a kid can be given even ten hours a week of work then it can grow to 20 hours, and then onwards from there after they’ve been given a start. It is better than having no job at all.”
Whether retailers will get any help in terms of their labour costs in the imminent UK budget was much debated the FT Live event. But of course no one knows yet what will be in the government’s economic plans. AI might not be beneficial either in terms of providing jobs in the future. But that debate - and the validity of whether it’s wise to tax the machines to provide a universal basic income for all, that people can then build on by their own job efforts if they want - wasn’t had in-situ either.
There is no doubting that it is a tough time for many retailers as cost-of-living pressures resurface for many consumers and high energy costs impact them. As ever though, good CX in whatever channel and good prices and propositions can still win out.

Juicy deals on TikTok Shop and drone delivery expansion in America: the retail technology week in numbers
Do you like numbers? Do you like retail tech news? Then this is the article for you. Including Walmart, Wing, Shopify, Snappy Shopper, Fenty Beauty, finmid, Kiehl’s, Procuros, YEEP!, Asos, VenHub Global, and the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards.
10…Asos customers received a push notification on 6th October, just before 10am, directing them to a Telegram account and informing them that the fast fashion online retailer had been hacked. The alleged hackers claimed they "compromised" Snowflake, but Asos later said it had found "no compromise" of its platform.
A statement noted that customers' personal information may have been accessed in the "unauthorised activity involving third-party platforms that we use to communicate with customers. We do not believe that payment card information or account passwords were impacted.”
£440 million...Retailers face a £440 million increase in electricity costs this year, despite their energy use remaining virtually unchanged, according to a new report from the British Retail Consortium (BRC). The trade body says it’s concerned that this will feed directly into consumer prices, raising the cost of living for millions of families.
The report notes that electricity costs are expected to rise from £2.72 billion in 2025 to £3.16 billion in 2026, an increase of 16% in just one year. Much of this rise is being driven by growing non-commodity charges (NCCs), government driven costs added to electricity bills, rather than global energy prices. These charges, which include government levies and rising and volatile network costs, now typically make up around two-thirds of retailers’ electricity bills. Transmission Network Use of System charges alone are expected to rise by 72%, adding almost £200 million to bills.
Retail is one of the UK’s major energy using industries and, following investment in decarbonisation, around 90% of the industry’s energy use now comes from electricity. This leaves retailers particularly exposed to rising electricity costs, with recent volatility in energy prices following conflict in the Middle East adding further pressure.
8...We're hugely pleased to present the finalists and shortlists for the eighth edition of the RTIH Innovation Awards, sponsored by 3D Cloud, Business France, and Retail Technology Show 2027. We received a record number of entries this year and many fantastic examples of technology excellence driving transformative change across the global retail sector

The event will be held on Wednesday, 4th November and consist of a drinks reception, three course meal, awards ceremony presided over by award winning stand-up comedian, presenter, actor and broadcaster, Aurie Styla, and after party until 1am.
Click here to book your place at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony on Wednesday, 4th November.
4,000...YEEP! reports that it has reached 4,000 parcel locker locations across the UK and is preparing to roll-out its new Generation 3 touchscreen lockers. The company, which operated just over 2,250 locations when Jamie Dickinson was appointed CEO in December last year, is now aiming to reach 5,000 by the end of 2026.
Developed with YEEP!’s hardware partner and shareholder kernTerminal, Generation 3 combines the company’s solar and battery powered technology with a new touchscreen interface designed to significantly improve the experience for both delivery drivers and consumers. All new YEEP! lockers will move to the Generation 3 specification from 2nd November, with a programme to upgrade the existing estate by end of Q1 2027.
Alongside the hardware, a bespoke operating system has been designed around the requirements of an open locker network. The system manages site surveys, installation, scheduling, maintenance and upgrades, with the aim of giving YEEP! greater visibility and control as the network scales.
€20 million...Hamburg-based software company Procuros has announced the closing of a €20 million Series A funding round led by XAnge, with W23 Global joining as a new investor. This takes total funding to date to €34 million.
Existing backers Point Nine, Creandum, SquareOne and b2venture are joining again, alongside several angel investors. Procuros will use the cash to accelerate its AI native supply chain connectivity platform and expand its trading network internationally. Over 300 companies are using Procuros, including Breuninger, Chefs Culinar, KoRo, flaconi, The Quality Group (ESN) and Hitschler, with more than €3 billion in annualised order volume said to be flowing through the platform.
“AI is advancing at incredible speed, while supply chains still run on infrastructure built decades ago. Operations teams are forced to bridge these gaps between systems that simply don’t communicate. We built Procuros to change that. Our infrastructure gives retailers, suppliers and AI agents the connectivity and trusted data they need to automate trade and make autonomous supply chains possible. Because ultimately, AI agents are only as good as the infrastructure they run on,” says Patrick Thelen, CEO and Co-Founder at Procuros.
"Procuros is showing that AI agents can make autonomous B2B trade a reality today. The team has built the infrastructure AI agents need to work across entire tradingnetworks and proven the model at scale in DACH. What excites us is the opportunity ahead: to take this beyond its home market and establish an entirely new category for global B2B trade,” says Valerie Bures-Bönström, Partner and Managing Director DACH at XAnge.
€17 million...Berlin-based embedded lending company, finmid, which is behind the financing programmes of Wolt, Delivery Hero and myPOS, has raised €17 million from Big Pi Ventures and Mainset, with Earlybird following on. The Series A extension brings total funding to date to €52 million.
The cash will be used to expand finmid's asset finance products, multi-source funding infrastructure and underwriting capabilities, and to support a move into vehicle financing and marketplace loans for the first time with Bolt and Skroutze. This is its first funding announcement since its €23 million Series A in April 2024.
Alexander Talkanitsa, Co-founder, says: "Two years ago, embedded lending meant a cash advance for a restaurant. Today the same rails carry a multi-year vehicle loan, a marketplace's own balance sheet, and the potential for more. Every platform with business customers now has a way to become their financing partner without becoming a bank."
53%...Consumers are entering the holiday season under significant economic pressure, with 53% of UK shoppers saying recent conditions have negatively affected their shopping plans. Planned Black Friday weekend spending across the UK is expected to drop to £165 on average from £181 in 2025.
A Shopify survey was conducted among 18,000 consumers in Australia, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, Spain, the UK and the US. And also 7,500 owners and business decision-makers across Australia, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, Spain, the UK and the US in companies with fewer than 1,000 employees.
One third of British shoppers have postponed a purchase in the past year because of increased living costs. To combat this, they are value-maxxing: spending more time researching, comparing and weighing up whether a purchase is genuinely worth it. 86% of Brits feel more in control after researching.
They’re also turning carts into watchlists. 28% said they deliberately leave products in their cart to see if the price drops. When shoppers did leave items in their carts, 32% said they return to complete the purchase when the price drops, while 29% buy after a discount code, voucher or special offer becomes available.

It says that this represents an important expansion of its technology into the multifamily residential market, where it reports growing demand from developers and property owners seeking new ways to enhance the resident experience and differentiate their communities.
“Multifamily residential communities represent a significant growth opportunity for VenHub, and we are seeing increasing demand from developers and property owners who recognise the value of bringing autonomous retail directly into their communities,” says Shahan Ohanessian, Founder and CEO at VenHub.

To date, the tie up has brought drone delivery access to more than three million customers across major US metropolitan areas, including Dallas-Fort Worth, Atlanta, Houston and Orlando.
“Adding new metros to our expansion speaks to how quickly people across the country are adopting drone delivery," says Heather Rivera, Chief Business Officer at Wing. “Expanding drone delivery to Seattle and Denver is about giving more customers a practical option when they need something quickly,” says Greg Cathey, Senior Vice President, eCommerce Transformation, Walmart. “Our stores put everyday items close to the communities we serve, and Wing helps bring those items to customers’ homes in minutes.”
1...Fenty Beauty, a cosmetics brand launched by singer Rihanna and luxury goods conglomerate LVMH, reports its first ever TikTok Shop LIVE. This took place on Monday, with an Instagram post promising “juicy deals, the chance to win exclusive freebies and more surprises”.
In a LinkedIn post, Amanda Uduku, a social commerce strategy advisor and former TikTok Partnerships Project Manager, said: “Rihanna is actually perfect for this, as she comes across funny and real, if you’ve seen her socials. I expect record numbers across the board, as this is as close fans will get to communicating with her (as long as they don’t ask about the album).”
“Also spotted, the brush she’s using in the announcement video is already linked, smart. Now that Meta is improving their social commerce capabilities, this will be the new way to get viewers to convert on both platforms. Why not increase sales potential, while getting fans excited for a shopping event? I think this method will reduce comments about what’s being used in the video and increase comments on how to use the products instead on Instagram. This is perfect for all categories, and to me says tutorial type content will increase going forward. Also, if this puts a stop to ‘comment Keyword to be sent the links’, then I’m all for it, bring back active comment sections.”
She concluded: “I’m ready to see Rihanna, the presenter. She’s not the first celebrity to do a TikTok Shop LIVE either. Both Nicki Minaj and Kim Kardashian have presented during their brand events (to name but a few), so I wonder who’s next?”

This spans three floors, and its design has been engineered to optimise customer flow, supporting an omnichannel experience that, according to the retailer, utilises in-store product showcases and exceptional customer service to drive brand loyalty.
It is only the second standalone boutique for Kiehl’s in the West End, joining 55 Monmouth Street, which was a recent upsize for the brand, also with Shaftesbury Capital.
William Oliver, Director of Retail and Restaurant Leasing at Shaftesbury Capital, says: “Bringing Kiehl’s to the heart of Carnaby Street strengthens a great partnership. Having worked closely with the brand on an upsize in Seven Dials, this new store ensures more visitors to the West End can explore and experience a quality offer, building brand loyalty and pointing to the power of having prime space as both a direct retail environment and showroom for the online customer. That Kiehl’s wanted to launch this European flagship on Carnaby Street, in its 175thyear, also highlights just how highly regarded the destination is, and how important it is for unmatched brand exposure and opportunity.”
Niki Lo, General Manager for Kiehl’s UK, says: "Carnaby Street is a legendary retail destination, and it is rapidly evolving into a key epicentre for beauty in London. Our continued investment in standout free-standing stores demonstrates our dedication to creating exceptional physical retail environments that drive high footfall and deep brand connection. This flagship allows us to reinforce our market share in the UK, partner more closely with our retail and real estate stakeholders, and deliver an elevated, best-in-class brand presence in one of Europe’s most vibrant commercial districts." the retail technology week in numbers

items.title: How to prevent the next Asos? Give businesses cybersecurity tax relief
items.summary: With Asos just the latest to be the victim of a cyber hack, it's time for the UK to start incentivising businesses to up their security.
items.body:
How to prevent the next Asos? Give businesses cybersecurity tax relief
With Asos just the latest big British retailer to be the victim of a cyber hack, it’s time for the government to start incentivising businesses to up their security, writes Matt Warman
On Tuesday, Asos customers across the UK were sent pop-up messages from its app that appeared to be from hackers.
The clothing giant will need time to figure out exactly what happened, but shoppers getting concerning messages through an app they trust will worry businesses, markets and our government.
And it should, because this story isn’t really about one retailer. Every few months we see another household name experiencing an attack: JLR and M&S for example. It isn’t just the private sector either: in July the Department for Education confirmed hackers had taken more than 600,000 records. Every time, we see it as an IT department issue when it’s a genuine economic problem. When systems go down, orders stop, services drop, shelves are empty and customers lose confidence.
To be fair to the government, its ambitions are the right ones as the Cyber Security and Resilience Bill, the Cyber Growth Action Plan and even cyber’s place in the Industrial Strategy all point in the right direction, building on cross-party work in Parliament in recent years. But calling something a priority without money behind it means very little.
When it comes to cybersecurity, there are three key things the government can do in the Budget which would genuinely make a difference.
How the government can back cyber
Firstly, we need to help businesses pay for protection before they’re targeted, and make it cheaper to buy. Right now, cybersecurity gets no direct tax relief and little in the way of incentives for UK businesses to invest more in it. Targeted relief or incentives on accredited products and services from UK providers would change that, and help the smaller firms who feel it’s too costly to try.
Secondly, we need to give small cyber firms a fair chance at public contracts as they make up 77 per cent of the whole cyber sector. They are also where some of the most innovative work in the UK is happening right now. The problem is that procurement still rewards whoever has the biggest bid team. We need to keep this in mind if we want to have a home-grown cyber industry, a key ambition of Burnham’s domestic supply chains.
Finally, we need to make sure there is support for organisations newly brought into scope by future legislation and regulation, so compliance costs don’t fall hardest on those least able to absorb them. Last month’s figures show 57 per cent of businesses now lack basic technical cyber skills, up from 49 per cent last year. Businesses cannot comply with rules nobody in the business understands. Funding for training and awareness alongside any new regulation and policy would make firms safer, and help them understand what’s being asked of them.
None of this is expensive by Budget standards, and it’s cheaper than the alternative. Last year’s attack on JLR cost the economy £1.9bn, needed a £1.5bn government loan guarantee and contributed to 4,000 job cuts. This won’t be a one-off. The National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) was dealing with four nationally significant attacks a week last year, and expects AI to increase both the number and impact of attacks. Without action, more of that bill could land on taxpayers.
As we wait for more information to come out on Asos, the ask for the Chancellor is clear: we need to pay for resilience now to avoid paying a lot more later. Invest in resilience, not consequence.
Matt Warman is chair of the Cybersecurity Business Network (CBN) and former UK digital and cyber minister

items.title: Harvey Nichols’ Birmingham store to close in January
items.summary: Closure will cost at least 60 jobs, while Leeds and Bristol outlets to be converted to Flannels brand Harvey Nichols’ Birmingham store is to close in January, with the loss of at least 60 jobs, while its Leeds and Bristol outlets will be converted to the Flannels brand in a shake-up under Mike Ashley’s Frasers Group. The owner of Sports Direct bought the department store chain , whose headquarters are at the Knightsbridge site in London, for £43m on the day it was put into administration in mid-August. Continue reading...
items.body:
Harvey Nichols’ Birmingham store is to close in January, with the loss of at least 60 jobs, while its Leeds and Bristol outlets will be converted to the Flannels brand in a shake-up under Mike Ashley’s Frasers Group.
The owner of Sports Direct bought the department store chain, whose headquarters are at the Knightsbridge site in London, for £43m on the day it was put into administration in mid-August.
About 1,000 of the group’s 1,200 jobs and six UK stores were saved in that deal. Harvey Nichols’ Oxo Tower restaurant was sold to a separate buyer, saving 130 jobs.
The chain’s branches in London, Edinburgh, Birmingham, Leeds and Manchester and Bristol are accompanied by outlets in Riyadh, Dubai, Doha, Kuwait and two in Hong Kong. A further store in Dublin was closed by administrators in September.
The Harvey Nichols Group owed about £100m to unsecured creditors at the time of its administration, including dozens of brands from Canada Goose to Victoria Beckham.
Ashley previously said he would keep Harvey Nichols’ Knightsbridge and Edinburgh stores, but rebrand the four other UK stores – in Birmingham, Leeds, Manchester and Bristol – as House of Fraser or Flannels.
It has now emerged that Frasers plans to close the Birmingham store, which opened 25 years ago, with staff informed earlier this week, as first reported by the fashion trade journal Drapers. Frasers will rebrand Leeds and Bristol to Flannels, while the future for the Manchester, Edinburgh and London Harvey Nichols stores is unclear.
Michael Murray, the chief executive of Frasers Group, recently said in a statement about the group’s luxury division: “Our ambition is clear: to continue scaling Frasers Group Luxury globally through organic expansion, acquisitions and strategic investments, creating long-term value for our brand partners, customers and the group.”
Ashley has bought a series of struggling premium brands in recent years after starting out with a single sports shop.
Frasers bought the House of Fraser department store chain out of administration in 2018 and has since closed about 40 of its 60 stores. It has been building its interests in luxury fashion with the Flannels chain and large stakes in brands such as the British handbag maker Mulberry.
The group recently celebrated lifting its stake in the German label Hugo Boss to 48%, just short of taking full control, despite opposition from the company’s board.
Frasers did not respond to a request for comment.

items.title: Asos hackers took more personal details than first revealed, BBC finds
items.summary: Retailer issues update after BBC contacted by cyber criminals who said this week's breach went beyond "basic contact details"
items.body:
Asos hackers took more personal details than first revealed, BBC finds
- Published
Asos has told its customers that hackers are in possession of detailed profiles of potentially millions of the online store's users.
It issued the update after BBC News told the retailer it had been contacted by cyber criminals who said this week's breach went beyond the "basic contact details" Asos previously said might have been accessed.
Names, addresses, phone numbers, emails, customer numbers and dates of birth are now in the hands of criminals.
One victim told the BBC it was "very unsettling" that the hackers now know these things about her.
The criminals also have access to the searches customers have made on the website. Terms like "reclaimed vintage", "glamorous wide fit" and "Asos petite" are visible in the data.
Harriet has been using Asos since 2019 - another detail the hackers now know.
"What I find particularly worrying is the possibility that stolen data can be used as a tool for for future attacks, meaning the impact of a breach could extend well beyond the initial incident," she said.
With the stolen information, scammers may be able to create convincing phishing attack emails or phone calls.
The risk to individuals is now higher and customers are being warned about potential impersonation scams.
In its email to customers, Asos confirmed data profiles were taken but said no bank details or passwords were accessed.
"Please remain cautious of unexpected messages or calls claiming to be from Asos," it said.
"We will never ask you to share passwords, security codes or payment details through an unsolicited message or call."
The company did not respond to questions about the scale of the breach.
The high profile hack made global headlines on Tuesday when cyber criminals used Asos's own app system to send a pop up notification to potentially millions of people.
Later that day the firm confirmed to shareholders via the London Stock Exchange that the pop up was sent by an "unauthorised third party" and "basic personal information including name and contact details may have been accessed."
The company then sent an email to customers with similar wording.
On Wednesday evening the cyber criminals responsible contacted the BBC sharing a sample of the stolen data which showed the true extent of the hack.
The BBC held off publishing this article to allow Asos to contact its customers first.
'Impersonating a trusted contact'
Asos said it is still investigating the data breach and it would "contact customers directly where we believe additional information, support or action may be required".
The UK fashion site explained to customers that hackers gained access to an Asos employee account by "impersonating a trusted contact to obtain log in credentials".
With that log in to an unnamed service, the hackers were able to download the customer data.
In the pop up notification send to customers by the hackers, they claimed they had "compromised the Snowflake instance".
Snowflake is a popular data storage and analysis company whose customers have been breached in the past due to unauthorised log ins.
The cyber criminals, calling themselves Xuanyewen, claimed to the BBC they used a platform which is built natively on top of Snowflake - called Simon AI - to gain access to the data.
Simon AI has been contacted for comment. Snowflake previously said its platform had not been breached.
Asos said customers are not being asked to take any action.
But cyber security experts have warned users to change passwords as a precaution and be on alert for suspicious activity.
"Passwords have not been stolen, so be highly suspicious of any unsolicited text or email asking you to change or share yours," said Trevor Dearing, Senior Director of Critical Infrastructure at Illumio.
"Expect scammers to mention the attack, use your personal details to seem genuine, and create urgency, such as threatening to lock your account within 24 hours."
Asos said its website and app are safe to use and "we know our customers trust us with their information".
"We take that responsibility seriously and have already taken additional steps to further strengthen security controls," it said.

items.title: Tesco predicts less boozy Christmas as weight-loss drugs and health drive hit demand for alcohol
items.summary: The boss of Tesco has said Brits are set to drink less booze this Christmas amid an increased interest in healthy lifestyles.
items.body:
Tesco predicts less boozy Christmas as weight-loss drugs and health drive hit demand for alcohol
The boss of Tesco has said Brits are set to drink less booze this Christmas amid an increased interest in healthy lifestyles.
Chief executive Ken Murphy said he believes there could be a ‘more moderate Christmas’ when it comes to drinking.
It comes as supermarkets and major food and drinks firms battle to adapt to a trend of people drinking less alcohol.
An increased uptake in people using weight-loss jabs is also thought to be influencing this. Medications such as Mounjaro can make drinking less appealing because it changes how the brain responds to pleasure as well as causing side effects including feeling sick.
But in addition to the popularity of such GLP-1 jabs, Murphy said the grocer was also seeing a ‘general trend toward healthier living’, which began during the Covid pandemic and continues to grow.
Tesco boss Ken Murphy said there could be a 'more moderate Christmas' when it comes to drinking this year.
He said: ‘I do think it could be a marginally healthier Christmas. Although customers do love to indulge, and we have planned accordingly.
‘We would say that there might be a more moderate Christmas from an alcohol point of view. We think low and no alcohol will see strong growth.’
The grocer has launched alcohol-free mocktail cans with flavours including Amaretto Sour, Passion Fruit and Pina Colada.
Murphy said weight-loss jabs were a 'component' of a 'broader trend', rather than a sole 'driver' of people drinking less and eating differently.
But Murphy said there would still be plenty of merriment across the UK this Christmas, with households set to splash out and indulge despite economic pressures.
He added: ‘I think that consumers, actually in the UK, have been pretty resilient in a very uncertain environment, and my sense is that customers will want to enjoy Christmas, given all that's going on in the world around them.’
And for those who find the prospect of a sober Christmas galling, Murphy said booze categories that he expects will boom include pre-mixed and ready-to-drink cocktails.
When it comes to food, customers are also seeking out products that contain high amounts of protein and fibre, he said.
This has influenced the company to increase its ranges of nutritious ready meals and high-fibre bakery goods.
Laura Tudor, trading manager of low and no alcohol at Waitrose, said sales in the category have risen 66 per cent over the past year.
She predicts that mocktails - cocktails that don’t have any alcohol in - will be popular over Christmas, with customers ‘looking for elevated options’ such as premium alcohol-free spirits and mixers. Searches for these types of drinks were up 325 per cent this month compared to last month, she added.
Drinks giant Diageo has launched a trial range of ‘mid-strength’ spirits, which have 20 per cent ABV compared to the standard 37.5 per cent. They have launched versions of Gordon's, Smirnoff and Captain Morgan.

items.title: Tesco narrows profit outlook as shoppers shrug off 'uncertainty' driven by the Middle East conflict
items.summary: Britain's largest grocer had said in April that it was giving a wider profit forecast than usual of between £3 billion and £3.30 billion, given the uncertainty caused by the war in the Middle East.
items.body:
Tesco narrows profit outlook as shoppers shrug off 'uncertainty' driven by the Middle East conflict
Tesco narrowed its profit guidance this morning as its 'relatively resilient' shoppers shrugged off economic pressures driven by the Middle East conflict.
Britain's largest grocer reported a 6.3 per cent increase in adjusted operating profit in the first half to £1.783billion even as unusually hot weather weighed on sales volumes.
Sales rose 1.6 per cent to £33.7 billion in the six months to 29 August.
Tesco had said in April that it was giving a wider profit forecast than usual - of between £3 billion and £3.3billion - given the uncertainty caused by the war in the Middle East.
But this morning it upped the lower end of this guidance, now steering profits between £3.15 billion and £3.30 billion.
'While consumer confidence has remained relatively resilient in the first half of the year, ongoing geopolitical tensions continue to create uncertainty, and we remain focused on helping customers get the best possible value from their weekly shop,' the supermarket said.
Chief executive Ken Murphy said he was feeling positive about Christmas
Shares rose 3.1 per cent to 490.7p as Tesco also announced an increase to its share buyback to £950 million, from £750 million.
Chief executive Ken Murphy said consumer resilience ‘is born out of dealing with kind of a series of external shocks and events and kind of uncertainty.’
‘They have to a certain extent become used to it, and they deal with it and they get on with life,’ he added, also pointing to the grocer’s efforts to keep prices low.'
That saw Tesco benefit from shoppers switching to its premium dine-in ranges as restaurant prices have put many off from eating out.
Its Finest ranges saw an 8.9 per cent sales increase as more than 350 new products have been launched, including a shake-up of bakery goods and new deli products. It expects Tesco Finest sales to top £3billion this year.
The results come days after it was revealed that Sainsbury’s and Morrisons ended talks over a potential billion-pound merger.
This would have created a giant with a 23.6 per cent market share - rivalling the 27.8 per cent share held by market leader Tesco, according to industry researchers Worldpanel.
Murphy said the business doesn’t ‘dwell too much’ on consolidation in the industry, when asked about the reports.
‘We're very focused on delivering our strategic plan. Whatever happens in the market, we'll respond to it - and really, our plan is to stay ahead through consistently investing in the business.’
Discounters Aldi and Lidl have poached market share from traditional supermarkets over the past few years.
Tesco has responded by adding more products in its Aldi price match as well as offering customers personalised offers through its Clubcard loyalty scheme.
The group is hoping to recapture a market share of 30 per cent, which it last recorded around 2013.
Murphy said the grocer had an ‘ambition to keep on growing’.
He said: ‘I was told six years ago that we had topped out and kind of life was over for Tesco. In the last four years, we have grown share by 113 basis points, which I think most people have been surprised by. So we like to surprise people.’
At its peak in 2007, Tesco accounted for almost £1 in every £3 spent at the checkout tills before dipping to a low of 25.6 per cent in 2020.
Tesco expects a less boozy Christmas
In addition to the rising uptake of GLP-1 weight-loss medications, Murphy said the grocer was also seeing a ‘general trend toward healthier living,’ with customers more interested in getting more protein and fibre.
This has influenced the company to increase its ranges of nutritious ready meals, no and low alcohol products and high-fibre bakery ranges.
Brits may be looking to make healthier choices and drink less booze this Christmas, Murphy said.
He said: ‘I do think it could be a marginally healthier Christmas. Although customers do love to indulge, and we have planned accordingly.’
‘We would say that there might be a more moderate Christmas from an alcohol point of view. We think low and no alcohol will see strong growth. We think cocktails will do well, and you'll see more sales of ready-to-drink and premixed cocktails.’
‘Usual suspects’ set to do well include a cheesecake dessert range and party food ranges including prawn toast, Murphy said.
Despite feeling 'optimistic and positive' as Tesco enters its critical Christmas trading period, Murphy renewed calls for shops to be given a reprieve on business rates at this month's Budget.
‘We have long argued that the rate system is fundamentally unfair. Retailers pay, on average, four times their fair share of rates.’
He said his ‘one ask’ of the Government going into the Budget is to exempt all retailers from a higher tax-paying band for commercial properties deemed at least £500,000 in rateable value.

Waitrose is celebrating the joy of a night in with a new campaign from Wonderhood Studios, spotlighting the supermarket’s premium No.1 £15 Dine In for Two and new No.1 £18 Takeaway for Four offers. The campaign taps into the familiar rituals of eating out through two 20-second films that appear to be set in restaurants, […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! items.body:
Waitrose is celebrating the joy of a night in with a new campaign from Wonderhood Studios, spotlighting the supermarket’s premium No.1 £15 Dine In for Two and new No.1 £18 Takeaway for Four offers.
The campaign taps into the familiar rituals of eating out through two 20-second films that appear to be set in restaurants, before revealing the diners are actually enjoying a Waitrose meal at home.
Both films close on the line ‘It’s not fine dining, it’s fine Dine In’, capturing the idea at the heart of the campaign: food that tastes so good, it brings the taste of a night out to a night at home.
In the first film, a couple enjoy what appears to be a meal out, before realising they need to get back for the babysitter. The reveal shows they haven’t gone anywhere at all – their baby is asleep on a monitor and they’re already at home enjoying Waitrose’s Dine In for Two.
The second sees a group of friends enjoying dinner together, with one particularly taken by the surroundings. As she compliments the décor, it becomes clear that the ‘restaurant’ she has been admiring is her own home.
The work builds on Waitrose’s ‘The home of food lovers’ platform, putting the supermarket front of mind for the end-of-week treat among 18-to-35-year-olds who might typically turn to a takeaway.
It shows how staying in can still deliver the great food, enjoyment and sense of occasion of a night out, while bringing value more visibly into the work, with the price of both offers featured prominently throughout the campaign.
The campaign was created by creatives Holly Nash and Alysha Radia, supported by creative directors James Rafter and Myles Vincent.
James Rafter, Creative Director at Wonderhood Studios, said: “The idea came directly from the food; and that was the Waitrose Dine In range is so good you’ll probably forget you’re at home in your slippers. The line “It’s not fine dining. It’s fine Dine In” was the perfect payoff for these films that showcase how a night in can feel like a treat even when you haven’t left home. More noodles, anyone?”
Myles Vincent, Creative Director at Wonderhood Studios, added: “The fun is in letting you think you know exactly where these dinners are happening, before pulling back to reveal no one has actually left the house. We played with all the familiar cues and rituals of eating out, then flipped them to show that the setting might be different, but the food doesn’t have to be.”
The campaign launches today across social and BVOD, supported by digital, OOH, and radio – including a partnership with Zoe Ball on Greatest Hits Radio, including live reads and a listener competition.
The films were produced by Wonderhood Makers, Wonderhood Studios’ in-house social content and production arm , and directed by Kyle Jon Shepherd. BVOD media was planned and bought by MG OMD, while social media was managed by Waitrose’s in-house team.

items.title: Small shops vital to DRS results, retailer tells Labour MPs
items.summary: Small independent retailers will be vital for the success or failure of the deposit return scheme (DRS) once it goes live in October 2027, a leading Fed member told Labour MPs, senior industry representatives and the deposit management organisation, Exchange for Change, during the recent… This story continues at Small shops vital to DRS results, retailer tells Labour MPs Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
But London member Kaual Patel, of Torridon Stores, in Catford, South East London, added that he and fellow retailers – particularly those who intended to participate voluntarily – needed clear advice and guidance.
Patel was speaking during a panel discussion that included Labour MPs Chris Bloore and Deirdre Costigan, as well as Zak Miller of CMB RVM company, Sam Jones of Coca-Cola Europacific Partners GB and Guy Mason representing Heineken.
The event took place on the second day of Labour’s conference at Albert Dock’s Premier Inn next to the River Mersey.
The active Fed member – who is already an established advocate of DRS – also repeated calls from the Fed’s Annual Conference in June for members to “start preparing as soon as possible”.
He said that whilst he acknowledged the costs associated with the scheme and setting up a reverse vending machine or manual return point, these could be dwarfed by lost business of 20-30% from footfall diverted to competitor businesses who participate in the scheme.
Calling for help and support from Exchange for Change, Patel continued: “My message is simple: retailers need clarity, guidance, and support from the scheme – particularly smaller retailers wanting to participate voluntarily.”
He also highlighted the importance of ensuring those smallest shops who are in urban areas with a floor area of less than 100sqm should be able to opt-in as easily as possible and that the voluntary registration process for these businesses should not be burdensome.
The need to help boost customer awareness of DRS was also stressed by Patel who called for a clear pricing system so that customers clearly understood the additional cost of the DRS deposit in bottle and can pricing to minimise any uncertainty or friction between retailers and their customers.
He spoke about the DRS trial currently running at his Catford business to boost local awareness but said that more needed to be done to help the public prepare.
The panel was overwhelmingly supportive of the scheme. However, Chris Bloore MP, who acts as chair of the Packaging in the Circular Economy All Party Parliamentary group, said there were real challenges associated with DRS and there was much to be learned from other countries, such as in Scandinavia which had DRS in place for many years and had achieved very high recycling return rates.

The Weston family brings a proven track record of enhancing […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! Retail Times - Retail Times, a free to view retail news website
items.body:
Following the announcement that the Weston family has agreed to acquire Boots from Sycamore Partners; Charlotte Chilcott, retail analyst at GlobalData, a leading intelligence and productivity platform, offers her view: “Boots is a strong, profitable business with genuine headroom for growth under the right stewardship. The Weston family brings a proven track record of enhancing retail businesses through investment and long-term ownership, such as their sustained operation and development of Shoppers Drug Mart across Canada as a leading pharmacy-led health and beauty retailer. The new owners should focus on refurbishing the full store estate and leveraging Boots’ health expertise to deliver a more consistent experience for consumers and sustainable growth for the business.
“Boots is uniquely strong in both health and beauty, setting the business apart from rivals such as Sephora and Space NK which focus exclusively on beauty. The Westons should leverage Boots’ reputation as a health expert, reinvesting in the pharmacy and health side of the business which has been deprioritised relative to beauty expansion. The Westons have proven they can position health expertise as a competitive differentiator through their operation of Shoppers Drug Mart in Canada. Applying this model to Boots, investing in more trained health advisors and enhanced clinical services, will bolster Boots’ health credentials and support revenue growth, whilst maintaining its growing beauty proposition. With increasing consumer demand for self-care, wellness and health-driven beauty, Boots is well positioned to capture growth across both categories.
“Store portfolio consistency should be another core focus. Flagship stores and larger locations have been revamped, but Boots operates a large network of smaller stores that have not seen the same level of investment and remain visually outdated. This inconsistency damages brand perception and frustrates shoppers. A disciplined programme to modernise smaller stores, by aligning design, merchandising and experience with flagship standards, will lift the brand image across the entire portfolio. This will mean a more consistent, pleasant shopping experience for consumers and drive traffic for the business in stores that currently underperform.

items.title: Tesco enters the second half with stronger profits and weaker sales momentum, says GlobalData
items.summary: Discover what's happening in retail today, Retail Times publishes international & UK retail news covering products, data, tech, packaging, people, research, comment and much more. Following today’s release of Tesco’s figures for the 26 weeks ending 29 August 2026; Eleanor Simpson-Gould, senior retail analyst at GlobalData, a leading intelligence and productivity platform, offers her view: “Tesco has delivered a mixed set of results; its profits are rising, but customers are holding back on spending. As the UK’s largest grocer, Tesco […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! Retail Times - Retail Times, a free to view retail news website
items.body:
Following today’s release of Tesco’s figures for the 26 weeks ending 29 August 2026; Eleanor Simpson-Gould, senior retail analyst at GlobalData, a leading intelligence and productivity platform, offers her view: “Tesco has delivered a mixed set of results; its profits are rising, but customers are holding back on spending. As the UK’s largest grocer, Tesco is a bellwether for the wider market, and H1 group sales growth slowing to 2.0% from 5.1% last year points to a broader drag on spending. This slower growth leaves little room once price inflation is accounted for, raising the prospect of volume declines across the market. UK like-for-like (l-f-l) sales decelerated through the half from 1.8% in Q1 to 1.3% in Q2. With Q2 including successive heatwaves and the World Cup, this should have lifted spending on drinks, barbecue food and at-home gatherings, yet the heat also worked against Tesco. Refrigeration failures at several stores during the summer heatwaves left chilled and frozen shelves empty and disrupted some home deliveries, which will have supressed sales.
“Profit performance however was strong, with Group adjusted operating profit up 6.5% to £1.8bn, as Tesco earned more from each shop through Finest trade-up, cost savings and newer income streams such as Tesco Media and Whoosh. On the back of this, Tesco has cautiously raised the lower end of its full-year profit guidance to £3.15bn, while keeping the upper end at £3.30bn. This signals confidence in the profit growth already secured, but limited visibility on demand and competition for the rest of the financial year.
“Premium own brand is increasingly propelling Tesco’s food growth. Food l-f-l sales rose 2.4%, while Finest sales grew 8.9%, demonstrating the grocer’s continued momentum in trading customers up even when spending is cautious. The supermarket retailer pushed hard on innovation during the half with 800+ new and improved products, including fibre-enriched bakery and high-protein ready meals. However, it must balance the volume of launches against the need to retain quality and convert impulse buys into repeat purchases. Tesco is leaning on Clubcard and AI to do this. Freebie Thursdays is a pragmatic sampling mechanism, but the AI meal-planning assistant, which it has now begun rolling out to customers, has greater strategic potential. It can build new lines and Finest products into planned weekly baskets, rather than relying on shoppers to discover them in the aisle. As we enter the festive season, Tesco should lead with fewer but higher-impact Finest launches, use Clubcard Prices to lower the barrier to trying them, and use the meal-planning assistant to build Finest products into customers’ Christmas menus.
“Non-food remains a drag on Tesco’s overall performance, with Home and Clothing l-f-l sales down 0.6%. TVs and collectables benefited from demand during the World Cup, but homewares categories were significantly weaker. Clothing is improving with less reliance on markdowns and better full-price performance. Towards the end of H1, Tesco launched its new F&F website and its improved discovery tools, such as “Shop the Look” and product videos, which could help lift clothing sales in H2 to offset weak home sales. Christmas is the immediate opportunity. Tesco must give gifting, partywear, and home textiles for festive hosting more prominence in large stores and on the F&F website. Tesco should also use Clubcard data to direct F&F offers to grocery shoppers who do not yet buy clothing or home products from Tesco, turning its food traffic into non-food sales.”

items.title: Asos says customers’ names, contact details and search histories hacked
items.summary: Experts say breadth of data accessed could help attackers devise “highly convincing” phishing scams Asos hackers gained access to millions of customers’ recent search histories as well as names, addresses and phone numbers, the online fashion retailer has revealed. Terms typed in by customers such as “glamorous wide fit” and “Asos petite” were in the data accessed in the cyber-attack, which emerged on Tuesday after app users received a notification titled “Asos hacked” with a link to the Telegram messaging service. Continue reading...
items.body:
Asos hackers gained access to millions of customers’ recent search histories as well as names, addresses and phone numbers, the online fashion retailer has revealed.
Terms typed in by customers such as “glamorous wide fit” and “Asos petite” were in the data accessed in the cyber-attack, which emerged on Tuesday after app users received a notification titled “Asos hacked” with a link to the Telegram messaging service.
After carrying out a “detailed, 48-hour investigation” into the incident, Asos confirmed on Thursday that basic personal information had been accessed by an unidentified third party. This included delivery and email addresses, names and phone numbers.
Experts said the extra information could help attackers devise “highly convincing” phishing scams targeted at customers.
Hackers gained access to a database of one of Asos’s third-party service providers by impersonating a “trusted contact” to gain access to one of its employee’s accounts, the retailer said.
Asos said they had also gained access to “certain non-personal account related information”, which are understood to include shoppers’ recent search history on the app, as first reported by the BBC which was contacted by the hackers.
Payment card details and passwords had not been accessed, the retailer added. It said in a message to customers on Thursday: “We discovered that an unauthorised party gained access to an Asos employee account by impersonating a trusted contact to obtain login credentials. Those credentials were then used to access information on certain third-party platforms used by Asos.
“The affected platforms were immediately locked down, ensuring that no further information could be accessed, and a full investigation was launched with the support of both internal and external cyber experts. We are also working with the relevant law enforcement and regulatory authorities.”
Asos said its website and app continued to be safe to use, that customers did not need to take action and that it had “already taken additional steps to further strengthen security controls”.
However, the company warned: “Please remain cautious of unexpected messages or calls claiming to be from Asos. We will never ask you to share passwords, security codes or payment details through an unsolicited message or call.”
Charles Allen, an analyst at Bloomberg Intelligence, said the hack might “temporarily cap the pace” of Asos’s attempt to revive sales and profits, after the Covid pandemic led to a period of boom followed by a sharp drop in trade. “The loss of customer trust could weigh on efforts to rebuild its client base,” he said.
Asos pledged to contact customers directly once its investigation was complete and “where we believe additional information, support or action may be required”.
The Telegram channel operated by the purported hackers, who have named themselves the Xuanye Group, to which users were directed on Tuesday carried a message assuring Asos customers that “payment information is not affected”.
Experts said they had not heard of the group before and that the push notification could have been an attempt to gain wider attention.
Simon Phillips, the chief technology officer at the cybersecurity firm CybaVerse, said the admission that a wider array of customer information was accessed than previously thought could lead to more persuasive phishing attempts.
“Given the information contained search data, and that Asos regularly sends customers reminder emails about the items they search for on the site, attackers could have used this data to send highly convincing scams which are disguised as the emails they typically receive from Asos,” he said.
Lisa Barber, the tech editor for the consumer watchdog Which?, said: “Shoppers should be especially wary of unexpected phone calls, texts, messages and emails they receive in the coming weeks and months.”
She said that if shoppers were unsure who they were speaking to, they should end the conversation and contact the company directly.
It is possible to dial 159 to speak to your bank’s fraud team, or use the number on the back of your card. If you have been called by a possible fraudster, wait at least 15 minutes before calling or use a different phone to ensure the scammer is no longer connected to the call, she said.
The hack comes after a number of British retailers, including Marks & Spencer, the Co-op and Harrods, suffered damaging cyber incidents last year. M&S and the Co-op experienced stock shortages, and the former was forced to shut down its website for several weeks while it ensured its systems were clean.

items.body:
weerapat1003 - stock.adobe.com
Scope of Asos data breach wider than first reported
Following a data breach earlier in October, cyber criminals appear to have a much more complete picture of Asos’ user base than first thought, it has emerged.
The scope of this week’s apparent breach of online retailer Asos’ mobile application appears to be much wider than was initially reported, with a BBC investigation finding that a significant amount of personally identifiable information (PII) was compromised.
The broadcaster said it was contacted by the cyber criminals who hijacked the app’s push notification feature to send messages to customers on Tuesday 6 October.
The gang, which goes by the name Xuanye, claimed it had accessed and stolen not only customer names and contact details such as addresses, emails and phone numbers, but also customer identification numbers and information on searches they made on the retailer’s app or website.
This could enable downstream cyber criminals and fraudsters to create much more detailed profiles of Asos’ customers, enabling more convincing phishing and social engineering attacks.
In an update to customers shared earlier today (Thursday 8 October), Asos said: “We’re sorry for the unauthorised notification some of you received on 6 October and any uncertainty this caused.
“Our priority will always be to protect our customers, to understand exactly what happened and to share accurate information as quickly as possible. Our teams, supported by external experts, have undertaken a detailed investigation over the last 48 hours.
“We discovered that an unauthorised party gained access to an Asos employee account by impersonating a trusted contact to obtain log-in credentials. Those credentials were then used to access information on certain third-party platforms used by Asos,” the fast-fashion retailer said.
“The affected platforms were immediately locked down, ensuring that no further information could be accesses and a full investigation was launched with the support of both internal and external cyber experts. We are also working with the relevant law enforcement and regulatory authorities.”
Asos said that names and contact details and certain “non-personal” account related information was compromised. It said that no payment card information, or account passwords were accessed, and insisted that its services remain safe to use.
It advised customers to remain cautious of unexpected messages or emails claiming to be from Asos.
“We know our customers trust us with their information. We take that responsibility seriously and have already taken additional steps to further strengthen security controls.
“Once our investigation is complete, we will contact customers directly where we believe additional information, support or action may be required,” it said.
The Asos incident appears to be the first major breach orchestrated by Xuanye – which some sources also style as Xuanyewen. According to the BBC’s reporting, the gang said that it had exploited an agentic marketing platform, Simon AI, which had access to Asos’ Snowflake instance. It is understood Snowflake has been conducting a parallel investigation of its own.
Crisis PR
Observers agreed that for Asos, the deepening severity of the incident heralds a potentially serious crisis, both in technological and reputational terms.
“There was no getting away from this one. It didn't sit in an inbox waiting to be read; it lit up the lock screens of app users, under the Asos name, before the company itself had a statement out,” said Camellia Chan, co-founder and CEO of X-Phy, an AI-backed data protection platform.
“That is what access to a retailer's communication platforms buys an attacker: a verified, engaged audience with purchase history attached. A message about a problem with this week's order sent under the retailer's brand will convert where a cold phishing email never would. The retailer has, in effect, assembled and qualified the victim pool, and the attackers only needed to borrow the keys. The names and contact details that were taken extend that reach by email and SMS long after the platform itself has been locked down.
“The route in matters as much as the data. The attackers did not need to break the storefront,” she added.
Hayley Goff, CEO of Whiteoaks International, a PR agency, said: “The latest revelations create a second challenge for Asos in maintaining customers’ confidence in what it tells them, as well as its ability to protect their information. With fuller disclosure following the BBC’s intervention, there is a risk customers feel the company is responding to scrutiny rather than keeping them informed.
“Investigations take time, but reassurance must keep pace with the evidence. Businesses need to distinguish clearly between what they have confirmed and what they are still investigating. When the picture changes, they must explain why,” said Goff.
“For Asos, the priority now is to make clear what the findings mean for customers and how it is addressing the risks. Every update is an opportunity to rebuild credibility or undermine it further.”
Learn more about IT at Asos
- Earlier this year, the Computer Weekly Downtime Upload podcast met to Przemek Czarnecki, chief technology officer at Asos, to discuss how the company is deploying AI and agentic AI.
- In 2022, we reported on how Asos was preparing to go deep into the Microsoft Azure cloud portfolio, as it looked to ramp up its use of data analytics to support its business growth goals.
- Amid the first Covid-19 lockdown, Asos rolled out augmented reality technology to let customers see how an outfit might look on them.

items.summary: Tesco posted its interim results today (8 October), covering the six months to 29 August 2026. While it shows a decline in sales for Booker, reflecting the impact of lapping strong growth in the prior year and the continued decline of the tobacco market, a… This story continues at Tesco reports ‘stable profit contribution’ from Booker in interim results Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
While it shows a decline in sales for Booker, reflecting the impact of lapping strong growth in the prior year and the continued decline of the tobacco market, a slight increase in operating profit was achieved via better buying terms and strong execution of Tesco’s ‘Save to Invest’ cost-efficiency program, effectively offsetting the drop in overall sales volumes
Booker’s total sales excluding tobacco was down 1.4%, while tobacco sales dropped 8.9% to £740m.
Traditional tobacco sales have been steadily declining due to regulatory changes, tax increases, and shifting consumer preferences toward vaping or quitting, while non-tobacco grocery categories continue to grow.
That is reflected throughout the sector with Tesco’s total convenience like-for-like sales (including One Stop stores) declining by 1.7% in the first half of fiscal year 2026, driven primarily by the continuing contraction in the tobacco market.
On a two-year basis, however, Booker, excluding tobacco, was up 2.7%.
Booker’s symbol brands (including Premier, Londis, Budgens, and Family Shopper) continued to deliver strong performance, supported by the addition of 275 net new retail partners during the period.
Despite lower overall volume, Tesco said the results demonstrate that Booker successfully managed its sales mix and operational costs to maintain a stable profit contribution to the Tesco Group.
Tesco Express sales were broadly flat year-on-year with performance supported by a 1.4 percentage points contribution from net new store openings.

Ocado Retail’s buying team has taken two lines: the Datekin Sukkari Pitted Dates Family Share Pack (12 […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! Retail Times - Retail Times, a free to view retail news website
items.body:
Datekin lands on Ocado.com, the world’s largest dedicated online supermarket, from 8th October, its first listing with a mainstream UK grocer, and the latest in a fast run of listings for the brand that launched in spring 2025.
Ocado Retail’s buying team has taken two lines: the Datekin Sukkari Pitted Dates Family Share Pack (12 x 30g, RRP £9.99) and Datekin Coconut & Tahini Date Balls (5-pack, RRP £2.49). Both launch on promotion at 33% off.
Ocado.com reaches over 80% of the UK population and serves more than 1 million active customers, with a range of around 50,000 products – putting Datekin in front of one of the largest online grocery audiences in the country.
The two lines going into Ocado.com are aimed at the household shop: twelve individually portioned 30g packs of soft, golden pitted Sukkari dates built for lunchboxes and packed lunches, and bite-sized pressed date balls with a roasted tahini centre rolled in desiccated coconut- both products are high in fibre, no added sugar, vegan and vegetarian.
The launch comes as new research* by the brand reveals a gap in Brits’ fibre knowledge. While one in three plan to eat more fibre in 2027, just 36% know how much they actually need. With adults advised to eat 30g a day, Datekin offers a simple way to boost fibre intake, with every product naturally high in fibre, making it an easy, everyday addition to the weekly shop.
Datekin launched in spring 2025 and has gone from a standing start to Selfridges, Amazon, more than 40 WHSmith Travel stores across the UK, and over 400 independent coffee shops and deli’s. In July, the brand picked up a one-star Great Taste award for its Date Filled Whole Wheat & Bran Cakes, and in September it won Best New Product for Food and Drink at the Glee trade show.
What sits behind the growth is owned supply and organic demand. Datekin’s dates are grown, handpicked and pitted on the founder’s family farms in Saudi Arabia – the brand’s direct supply chain is vital at a time when the wider category is wrestling with shortages and shipping costs. Increased organic demand from shoppers for a more natural snacking range has been apparent with shoppers looking for a clean and simple ingredients list, which Datekin can meet with the latest range going into Ocado only having 1 to 3 ingredients.
Megan Matthews, head of marketing at Datekin, said: “We’ve moved quickly since launching in spring 2025, and the reason we’ve been able to is that we own our farms and hold our stock here in the UK. That’s what lets us say yes to a retailer like Ocado. Their buyers can see the growth of the natural snacking category, and they’ve chosen to back both our Family Share Pack and our coconut date balls from day one – this is the listing that puts Datekin into the weekly online shop. ”
Lily Bentley, snacks & nuts buyer at Ocado.com, added: “I am excited to introduce Datekin to Ocado’s snack range, launching two of their products! Demand for high-fibre, whole-food options continues to grow, and Datekin’s products align well with what our customers are looking for – combining clean-label ingredients with functional health benefits.”
